# can be rounded once it is known closely enough. Each function computes N
# with |N / 2^F - f(x)| < 2^16 / 2^F (every truncation is at most one unit
# and far fewer than 2^16 occur), rounds N - 2^16 and N + 2^16, and
# returns when both round to the same double; otherwise F grows (200, 500,
# 1000, 2000 bits). CORE-MATH uses the same two-phase idea with
# double-double fast paths; here every phase is exact integer arithmetic,
# so its correctness does not rest on a worst-case table. Integers are
# magnitudes in base 2^30 limbs.

const LB: i64 = 30
const LM: i64 = 1073741823
const EB: i64 = 65536

fn n_trim(a: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o = a
while o.len() > 0 and o[o.len() - 1] == 0 bound 1048576
let _ = o.pop()
return o

fn n_of(v: i64) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
var x = v
while x > 0 bound 4
o.push(x & LM)
x = x >> LB
return o

fn n_to_i64(a: &[i64]) -> i64
var v: i64 = 0
var i = a.len()
while i > 0 bound 3
i -= 1
v = (v << LB) + a[i]
return v

fn n_cmp(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> i64
if a.len() != b.len()
return if a.len() < b.len() then -1 else 1
var i = a.len()
while i > 0 bound 1048576
i -= 1
if a[i] != b[i]
return if a[i] < b[i] then -1 else 1
return 0

fn n_add(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
var c: i64 = 0
let n = if a.len() > b.len() then a.len() else b.len()
for i in 0..n
var s = c
if i < a.len()
s += a[i]
if i < b.len()
s += b[i]
o.push(s & LM)
c = s >> LB
if c > 0
o.push(c)
return o

# a - b, a >= b
fn n_sub(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
var br: i64 = 0
for i in 0..a.len()
var s = a[i] - br
if i < b.len()
s -= b[i]
if s < 0
s += LM + 1
br = 1
else
br = 0
o.push(s)
return n_trim(o)

fn n_mul(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
if a.len() == 0 or b.len() == 0
return []
var o: List[i64] = []
for _k in 0..(a.len() + b.len())
o.push(0)
for i in 0..a.len()
var c: i64 = 0
for j in 0..b.len()
let t = o[i + j] + a[i] * b[j] + c
o[i + j] = t & LM
c = t >> LB
o[i + b.len()] = c
return n_trim(o)

# a * s, 0 <= s < 2^30
fn n_muls(a: &[i64], s: i64) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
var c: i64 = 0
for x in a
let t = x * s + c
o.push(t & LM)
c = t >> LB
while c > 0 bound 4
o.push(c & LM)
c = c >> LB
return n_trim(o)

# floor(a / s), 0 < s < 2^30
fn n_divs(a: &[i64], s: i64) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
for _k in 0..a.len()
o.push(0)
var r: i64 = 0
var i = a.len()
while i > 0 bound 1048576
i -= 1
let t = (r << LB) + a[i]
o[i] = t / s
r = t % s
return n_trim(o)

fn n_shr(a: &[i64], s: i64) -> List[i64]
let q = (s / LB) as usize
let b = s % LB
var o: List[i64] = []
var i = q
while i < a.len() bound 1048576
var v = a[i] >> b
if b > 0 and i + 1 < a.len()
v = v | ((a[i + 1] << (LB - b)) & LM)
o.push(v)
i += 1
return n_trim(o)

fn n_shl(a: &[i64], s: i64) -> List[i64]
let q = s / LB
let b = s % LB
var o: List[i64] = []
for _k in 0..q
o.push(0)
var c: i64 = 0
for x in a
o.push(((x << b) & LM) | c)
c = if b > 0 then x >> (LB - b) else 0
o.push(c)
return n_trim(o)

# the low s bits of a
fn n_low(a: &[i64], s: i64) -> List[i64]
let q = (s / LB) as usize
let b = s % LB
var o: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 0
while i < a.len() and i <= q bound 1048576
if i < q
o.push(a[i])
else
o.push(a[i] & ((1 << b) - 1))
i += 1
return n_trim(o)

fn n_bits(a: &[i64]) -> i64
if a.len() == 0
return 0
var t = a[a.len() - 1]
var n: i64 = 0
while t > 0 bound 31
t = t >> 1
n += 1
return ((a.len() - 1) as i64) * LB + n

fn n_bit(a: &[i64], i: i64) -> bool
let q = (i / LB) as usize
if q >= a.len()
return false
return ((a[q] >> (i % LB)) & 1) == 1

# floor(a 2^f / b), b > 0, exactly: a Newton reciprocal Y ~ 2^K / b
# (from a double start, doubling its bits per step) gives an estimate that
# the remainder then corrects to the exact floor.
fn n_div(a: &[i64], b: &[i64], f: i64) -> List[i64]
let num = n_shl(a, f)
let lb = n_bits(b)
let k = n_bits(&num) + 64
# Y0 from the top 53 bits of b
let sh = lb - 53
let bt = if sh >= 0 then n_shr(b, sh) else n_shl(b, 0 - sh)
let r53 = (1.0 / (n_to_i64(&bt) as f64)) * pow2(105)
let y0 = n_of(r53 as i64)
var y = if k - sh >= 105 then n_shl(&y0, k - sh - 105) else n_shr(&y0, 105 - k + sh)
let two = n_pow2(k + 1)
var prec: i64 = 48
while prec < k - lb + 8 bound 64
let t = n_mul(b, &y)
let d = if n_cmp(&two, &t) > 0 then n_sub(&two, &t) else []
let yd = n_mul(&y, &d)
y = n_shr(&yd, k)
prec = prec * 2
let qa = n_mul(&num, &y)
var q = n_shr(&qa, k)
var qb = n_mul(&q, b)
let one = [1]
while n_cmp(&qb, &num) > 0 bound 1048576
q = n_sub(&q, &one)
qb = n_sub(&qb, b)
var rem = n_sub(&num, &qb)
while n_cmp(&rem, b) >= 0 bound 1048576
q = n_add(&q, &one)
rem = n_sub(&rem, b)
return q

fn n_pow2(s: i64) -> List[i64]
let one = [1]
return n_shl(&one, s)

# N * 2^sh rounded to nearest even binary64 (subnormals included); an
# overflowing value traps (non-finite result).
fn n_round(n: &[i64], sh: i64) -> f64
let l = n_bits(n)
if l == 0
return 0.0
let e = l - 1 + sh
if e > 1023
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
var drop = l - 53
if e < -1022
drop = -1074 - sh
if drop <= 0
return (n_to_i64(n) as f64) * pow2(sh)
let qn = n_shr(n, drop)
var q = n_to_i64(&qn)
if n_bit(n, drop - 1)
let rest = n_low(n, drop - 1)
if rest.len() > 0 or q % 2 == 1
q += 1
return (q as f64) * pow2(sh + drop)

# x = M 2^E exactly, M < 2^53 an integer, for normal x > 0: [M, E]
# (exp and sin/cos only take it for |x| > 2^-60)
fn mant(x: f64) -> List[i64]
let fr = frexp1(x)
return [(fr[0] * P52) as i64, (fr[1] as i64) - 52]

# The value of the Ziv loop: [lo, hi] doubles of N -+ EB at scale 2^sh.
fn ziv(n: &[i64], sh: i64) -> List[f64]
let eb = n_of(EB)
return ziv_eb(n, sh, &eb)

# ... with an explicit error bound eb (same units as N).
fn ziv_eb(n: &[i64], sh: i64, eb: &[i64]) -> List[f64]
if n_cmp(n, eb) <= 0
return [0.0, 1.0]
let lo = n_sub(n, eb)
let hi = n_add(n, eb)
return [n_round(&lo, sh), n_round(&hi, sh)]

fn cst(c: &[i64], bits: i64, f: i64) -> List[i64]
return n_shr(c, bits - f)

# x as a fixed-point magnitude with f fraction bits (exact when f is large
# enough for x's last bit).
fn fix(x: f64, f: i64) -> List[i64]
let me = mant(fabs(x))
let m = n_of(me[0])
if me[1] + f >= 0
return n_shl(&m, me[1] + f)
return n_shr(&m, 0 - me[1] - f)

const ZIV_F: List[i64] = [200, 500, 1000, 2000]

# ---- exp ----------------------------------------------------------------
# x = k ln2 + r, 0 <= r < ln2, exp(x) = exp(r) 2^k.

# exp(r) for 0 <= r < 1 at f fraction bits (Taylor)
fn exp_fix(r: &[i64], f: i64) -> List[i64]
var s = n_pow2(f)
var t = n_pow2(f)
var k: i64 = 1
while t.len() > 0 bound 4096
let p = n_mul(&t, r)
let ps = n_shr(&p, f)
t = n_divs(&ps, k)
s = n_add(&s, &t)
k += 1
return s

pub fn exp(x: f64) -> f64
if x == 0.0
return 1.0
if fabs(x) < 5.551115123125783e-17
return 1.0
if x > 709.7827128933841
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
if x < -745.2
return 0.0
for f in ZIV_F
let xf = fix(x, f)
let c = c_ln2()
let l = cst(&c, 2100, f)
var k = (fabs(x) / 0.6931471805599453).floor() as i64
if x < 0.0
k += 1
var kl = n_muls(&l, k)
while x >= 0.0 and n_cmp(&kl, &xf) > 0 bound 4
k -= 1
kl = n_muls(&l, k)
while x < 0.0 and n_cmp(&kl, &xf) < 0 bound 4
k += 1
kl = n_muls(&l, k)
let r = if x >= 0.0 then n_sub(&xf, &kl) else n_sub(&kl, &xf)
let e = exp_fix(&r, f)
let kk = if x >= 0.0 then k else 0 - k
let z = ziv(&e, kk - f)
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# ---- log ----------------------------------------------------------------
# x = m 2^e, m in [0.75, 1.5), log x = e ln2 + 2 atanh((m-1)/(m+1)).

# 2 atanh(z) for |z| = num / den < 1/4 (num, den < 2^55): f fraction bits
fn log_fix(num: i64, den: i64, f: i64) -> List[i64]
# long division, 6 bits per step (r < den < 2^55, so r 2^6 < 2^63)
var z: List[i64] = []
var r = num
var w: i64 = 0
var p: i64 = 0
var got: i64 = 0
var digits: List[i64] = []
while got < f bound 1048576
let t = r << 6
digits.push(t / den)
r = t % den
got += 6
# digits[0] holds bits 2^-1..2^-6; floor(z 2^got) little-endian
var i = digits.len()
while i > 0 bound 1048576
i -= 1
w = w | (digits[i] << p)
p += 6
if p == LB
z.push(w)
w = 0
p = 0
z.push(w)
z = n_shr(&z, got - f)
return atanh2_fix(&z, f)

# 2 atanh(z) = 2 (z + z^3/3 + ...) for 0 <= z / 2^f < 1/4: f fraction bits
fn atanh2_fix(z: &[i64], f: i64) -> List[i64]
let zz = n_mul(z, z)
let z2 = n_shr(&zz, f)
var s = n_shr(z, 0)
var t = n_shr(z, 0)
var k: i64 = 1
while t.len() > 0 bound 4096
let p = n_mul(&t, &z2)
t = n_shr(&p, f)
k += 2
let d = n_divs(&t, k)
s = n_add(&s, &d)
return n_muls(&s, 2)

# which: 0 log, 1 log2, 2 log10. value = e K + log(m) S with (K, S) =
# (ln 2, 1), (1, log2 e), (log10 2, log10 e).
fn log_gen(x: f64, which: i64) -> f64
if x <= 0.0
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
if x == 1.0
return 0.0
let fr = frexp1(x)
var m = fr[0]
var e = fr[1] as i64
if m >= 1.5
m = m * 0.5
e += 1
# m in [0.75, 1.5): M = m 2^53 exactly
let mm = (m * P52 * 2.0) as i64
let one: i64 = 9007199254740992
let neg = mm < one
let num = if neg then one - mm else mm - one
let den = mm + one
for f in ZIV_F
var lm = if num == 0 then [] else log_fix(num, den, f)
var kc = c_ln2()
if which == 1
let sc = c_log2e()
let s1 = cst(&sc, 2100, f)
let p1 = n_mul(&lm, &s1)
lm = n_shr(&p1, f)
kc = n_pow2(2100)
elif which == 2
let sc = c_log10e()
let s1 = cst(&sc, 2100, f)
let p1 = n_mul(&lm, &s1)
lm = n_shr(&p1, f)
kc = c_log10_2()
let l = cst(&kc, 2100, f)
let el = n_muls(&l, if e < 0 then 0 - e else e)
# value = e K + (neg ? -lm : lm)
let a_neg = e < 0
var res: List[i64] = []
var rneg = false
if a_neg == neg
res = n_add(&el, &lm)
rneg = neg
elif n_cmp(&el, &lm) >= 0
res = n_sub(&el, &lm)
rneg = a_neg
else
res = n_sub(&lm, &el)
rneg = neg
let z = ziv(&res, 0 - f)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if rneg then 0.0 - z[0] else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

pub fn log(x: f64) -> f64
return log_gen(x, 0)

pub fn log2(x: f64) -> f64
return log_gen(x, 1)

pub fn log10(x: f64) -> f64
return log_gen(x, 2)

# ---- sin, cos -------------------------------------------------------------
# Payne-Hanek: x = M 2^E times 2/pi (4200 bits), mod 4, exact for every
# finite x (the error is below 2^-3000 at x = 2^1024), then q pi/2 +- r with
# 0 <= r <= pi/4.

# [sin r, cos r] at f fraction bits for 0 <= r <= pi/4 (Taylor, alternating
# series summed as positive and negative parts)
fn sincos_fix(r: &[i64], f: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let rr = n_mul(r, r)
let r2 = n_shr(&rr, f)
var sp = copy(r)
var sn: List[i64] = []
var t = copy(r)
var k: i64 = 1
var plus = false
while t.len() > 0 bound 4096
let p = n_mul(&t, &r2)
let ps = n_shr(&p, f)
t = n_divs(&ps, (k + 1) * (k + 2))
k += 2
if plus
sp = n_add(&sp, &t)
else
sn = n_add(&sn, &t)
plus = not plus
var cp = n_pow2(f)
var cn: List[i64] = []
t = n_pow2(f)
k = 0
plus = false
while t.len() > 0 bound 4096
let p = n_mul(&t, &r2)
let ps = n_shr(&p, f)
t = n_divs(&ps, (k + 1) * (k + 2))
k += 2
if plus
cp = n_add(&cp, &t)
else
cn = n_add(&cn, &t)
plus = not plus
return [n_sub(&sp, &sn), n_sub(&cp, &cn)]

# which: 0 sin, 1 cos
fn trig(x: f64, which: i64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax < 7.450580596923828e-09
if which != 1
return x
return 1.0
let me = mant(ax)
let mn = n_of(me[0])
let tp = c_two_opi()
let t = n_mul(&mn, &tp)
for f in ZIV_F
# q + h = x 2/pi mod 4 with f fraction bits
let ws = n_shr(&t, 4200 - me[1] - f)
let w = n_low(&ws, f + 2)
let qn = n_shr(&w, f)
var q = n_to_i64(&qn)
var h = n_low(&w, f)
var minus = false
if n_bit(&h, f - 1)
let one = n_pow2(f)
h = n_sub(&one, &h)
q = (q + 1) % 4
minus = true
let c = c_pio2()
let pc = cst(&c, 2100, f)
let hp = n_mul(&h, &pc)
let r = n_shr(&hp, f)
let sc = sincos_fix(&r, f)
# sin(q pi/2 +- r), cos(q pi/2 +- r)
var useS = false
var neg = false
if which == 0
useS = q % 2 == 0
neg = q >= 2
if useS and minus
neg = not neg
else
useS = q % 2 == 1
neg = q == 1 or q == 2
if useS and minus
neg = not neg
if which == 2
# tan(q pi/2 +- r): tan r (q even) or -cot r (q odd), so the
# quotient's error grows like (1 + Q^2): bound it from Q
let even = q % 2 == 0
let s0 = copy(sc[0])
let s1 = copy(sc[1])
let tq = if even then n_div(&s0, &s1, f) else n_div(&s1, &s0, f)
let qi = n_shr(&tq, f)
let one = [1]
let q1 = n_add(&qi, &one)
let qq = n_mul(&q1, &q1)
let e2 = n_muls(&qq, 2 * EB)
let e4 = n_of(4 * EB)
let eb = n_add(&e2, &e4)
let z = ziv_eb(&tq, 0 - f, &eb)
if z[0] == z[1]
var s = if even then minus else not minus
if x < 0.0
s = not s
return if s then 0.0 - z[0] else z[0]
continue
let v = if useS then copy(sc[0]) else copy(sc[1])
if v.len() > 0
let z = ziv(&v, 0 - f)
if z[0] == z[1]
let s = if x < 0.0 and which == 0 then not neg else neg
return if s then 0.0 - z[0] else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

pub fn sin(x: f64) -> f64
return trig(x, 0)

pub fn cos(x: f64) -> f64
return trig(x, 1)

pub fn tan(x: f64) -> f64
return trig(x, 2)

# ---- atan2 -------------------------------------------------------------
# t = min(|x|,|y|) / max(|x|,|y|) <= 1 as an exact quotient; atan(t) =
# atan(j/64) + atan(u), j = round(64 t), u = (t - j/64) / (1 + t j/64),
# |u| <= 1/128, Taylor. Then pi/2 - a, pi - a and the signs.

fn negz(x: f64) -> bool
return x == 0.0 and (x as f32).tostr() == "-0"

fn is_neg(x: f64) -> bool
return x < 0.0 or negz(x)

# x = M 2^E exactly for any x > 0, subnormals included
fn mant_any(x: f64) -> List[i64]
if x < 2.2250738585072014e-308
return [(x * pow2(600) * pow2(474)) as i64, -1074]
return mant(x)

# atan(t) for 0 <= t <= 1 at fe fraction bits (fe <= 2100 when t >= 1/128)
fn atan_fix(t: &[i64], fe: i64) -> List[i64]
let half = n_pow2(fe - 7)
let tj = n_add(t, &half)
let jn = n_shr(&tj, fe - 6)
let j = n_to_i64(&jn)
var u = copy(t)
var uneg = false
var base: List[i64] = []
if j > 0
let jj = n_of(j)
let c = n_shl(&jj, fe - 6)
let tc = n_mul(t, &c)
let tcs = n_shr(&tc, fe)
let one = n_pow2(fe)
let den = n_add(&one, &tcs)
uneg = n_cmp(t, &c) < 0
let num = if uneg then n_sub(&c, t) else n_sub(t, &c)
u = n_div(&num, &den, fe)
let tab = c_atan_tab()
var e: List[i64] = []
for i in 0..71
e.push(tab[((j - 1) * 71 + i) as usize])
let et = n_trim(e)
base = n_shr(&et, 2100 - fe)
# atan(u) = u - u^3/3 + u^5/5 - ...
let uu = n_mul(&u, &u)
let u2 = n_shr(&uu, fe)
var sp = copy(u)
var sn: List[i64] = []
var p = copy(u)
var k: i64 = 1
var plus = false
while p.len() > 0 bound 4096
let pm = n_mul(&p, &u2)
p = n_shr(&pm, fe)
k += 2
let d = n_divs(&p, k)
if plus
sp = n_add(&sp, &d)
else
sn = n_add(&sn, &d)
plus = not plus
let a = n_sub(&sp, &sn)
if uneg
return n_sub(&base, &a)
return n_add(&base, &a)

pub fn atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64
let yneg = is_neg(y)
let xneg = is_neg(x)
if y == 0.0
if xneg
return if yneg then 0.0 - 3.141592653589793 else 3.141592653589793
return y
if x == 0.0
return if yneg then 0.0 - 1.5707963267948966 else 1.5707963267948966
let ay = fabs(y)
let ax = fabs(x)
let swap = ay > ax
let mn = if swap then mant_any(ax) else mant_any(ay)
let md = if swap then mant_any(ay) else mant_any(ax)
let d = md[1] - mn[1]
let a1 = n_of(mn[0])
let b1 = n_of(md[0])
for f in ZIV_F
let r = atan_core(&a1, &b1, 0 - d, d, swap, xneg, f)
let z = ziv(&r[1], 0 - r[0][0])
if z[0] == z[1]
return if yneg then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# [[fe], N]: N / 2^fe = atan(t) (swap false) or pi/2 - atan(t) (swap true),
# then pi minus that when xneg, for t = (a / b) 2^sh <= 1 known exactly;
# 2^-d ~ t. A tiny result keeps its relative precision, and atan(t) =
# t - t^3/3 can sit within t^3 of a rounding midpoint (t = 2^-1075 is
# one), so 3d more fraction bits for t ~ 2^-d once the first try failed.
fn atan_core(a: &[i64], b: &[i64], sh: i64, d: i64, swap: bool, xneg: bool, f: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let dd = if f == 200 then d else 3 * d
let fe = if not swap and not xneg and d > 0 then f + dd else f
let t = if fe + sh >= 0 then n_div(a, b, fe + sh) else []
var r = atan_fix(&t, fe)
if swap
let c = c_pio2()
let pc = cst(&c, 2100, fe)
r = n_sub(&pc, &r)
if xneg
let c = c_pio2()
let pc = cst(&c, 2100, fe)
let pi = n_muls(&pc, 2)
r = n_sub(&pi, &r)
return [[fe], r]

# ---- atan, asin, acos -----------------------------------------------------

pub fn atan(x: f64) -> f64
return atan2(x, 1.0)

# floor(sqrt(n)): Newton from a power of two above it, decreasing until fixed
fn n_isqrt(n: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
let l = n_bits(n)
if l == 0
return []
# start just above sqrt from the top 52..53 bits (an even shift)
let sh = if l > 53 then (l - 52) / 2 * 2 else 0
let tn = n_shr(n, sh)
let st = (n_to_i64(&tn) as f64).sqrt() * 1.000000001 + 2.0
let s0 = n_of(st as i64)
var s = n_shl(&s0, sh / 2)
var go = true
while go bound 4096
let q = n_div(n, &s, 0)
let t = n_add(&s, &q)
let s2 = n_shr(&t, 1)
if n_cmp(&s2, &s) < 0
s = s2
else
go = false
return s

# asin / acos: x = M 2^E, |x| < 1, so 1 - x^2 = D 2^(2E) with D = 2^(-2E) - M^2
# exact, and with S = floor(sqrt(D 2^(2g))) both are atan of a ratio of
# integers: asin x = atan(M 2^g / S), acos x = atan2(S, M 2^g). S is off by
# under one part in 2^g, which moves atan by under 2^-g: g = f + 160 is far
# below the Ziv bound at fe <= f + 3d (d <= 81 here).
fn asin_acos(x: f64, ac: bool) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
let m = mant_any(ax)
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let m2 = n_mul(&mm, &mm)
let p = n_pow2(0 - 2 * m[1])
let dn = n_sub(&p, &m2)
for f in ZIV_F
let g = f + 160
let dg = n_shl(&dn, 2 * g)
let sq = n_isqrt(&dg)
let mg = n_shl(&mm, g)
let c = if ac then n_cmp(&sq, &mg) else n_cmp(&mg, &sq)
let swap = c > 0
let d = if swap == ac then n_bits(&sq) - n_bits(&mg) else n_bits(&mg) - n_bits(&sq)
let xn = ac and x < 0.0
let r = if swap == ac then atan_core(&mg, &sq, 0, d, swap, xn, f) else atan_core(&sq, &mg, 0, d, swap, xn, f)
let z = ziv(&r[1], 0 - r[0][0])
if z[0] == z[1]
return if not ac and x < 0.0 then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# asin x ~ x + x^3/6 rounds to x for |x| < 2^-28; |x| > 1 traps
pub fn asin(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax > 1.0
return 0.0 / 0.0
if ax == 1.0
return if x < 0.0 then 0.0 - 1.5707963267948966 else 1.5707963267948966
if ax < 3.725290298461914e-09
return x
return asin_acos(x, false)

pub fn acos(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax > 1.0
return 0.0 / 0.0
if x == 1.0
return 0.0
if x == -1.0
return 3.141592653589793
# pi/2 - x: the double nearest pi/2 is 6.1e-17 below it, so for
# |x| < 2^-55 the result stays within 8.9e-17 < ulp/2 of it
if ax < 2.7755575615628914e-17
return 1.5707963267948966
if ax < 0.0009765625
return acos_small(x)
return asin_acos(x, true)

# acos x = pi/2 -+ asin |x| for |x| < 2^-10, asin by its series
# sum (2k)!/(4^k k!^2 (2k+1)) x^(2k+1) in G-bit fixed point (term ratio
# under 2^-20, each term off by under 2 units, about G/20 terms): no
# square root, so tiny |x| costs O(G^2 / 20) instead of a 2G-bit isqrt
fn acos_small(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
for f in ZIV_F
let gg = f + 64
let xf = fix(ax, gg)
let xx = n_mul(&xf, &xf)
let x2 = n_shr(&xx, gg)
var t = n_shr(&xf, 0)
var s = n_shr(&xf, 0)
var k: i64 = 0
while t.len() > 0 bound 4096
k += 1
let tx = n_mul(&t, &x2)
let tp = n_shr(&tx, gg)
let tq = n_muls(&tp, (2 * k - 1) * (2 * k - 1))
t = n_divs(&tq, 2 * k * (2 * k + 1))
s = n_add(&s, &t)
let c = c_pio2()
let pc = cst(&c, 2100, gg)
let v = if x < 0.0 then n_add(&pc, &s) else n_sub(&pc, &s)
let z = ziv(&v, 0 - gg)
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0


# ---- sinh, cosh, tanh -------------------------------------------------------
# e^|x| = N1 2^(k1 - g), e^-|x| = N2 2^(k2 - g) (exp_big), so with
# N2' = N2 / 2^(k1 - k2): sinh, cosh = (N1 -+ N2') 2^(k1 - 1 - g) and
# tanh = (N1 - N2') / (N1 + N2'). g = f + ex + 64 keeps f bits relative to
# the result through the cancellation (ex ~ log2(1 / |x|) <= 27).
fn hyp_parts(ax: f64, g: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let xf = fix(ax, g)
let p = exp_big(false, &xf, g)
let q = exp_big(true, &xf, g)
let k1 = p[0][0]
let n2 = n_shr(&q[1], k1 - q[0][0])
return [[k1], n_sub(&p[1], &n2), n_add(&p[1], &n2)]

fn hyp_ex(ax: f64) -> i64
let fr = frexp1(ax)
let e = fr[1] as i64
return if e < 0 then 0 - e else 0

# which: 0 sinh, 1 cosh
fn sinh_cosh(x: f64, which: i64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax > 711.0
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
let ex = hyp_ex(ax)
for f in ZIV_F
let g = f + ex + 64
let h = hyp_parts(ax, g)
let z = if which == 0 then ziv(&h[1], h[0][0] - 1 - g) else ziv(&h[2], h[0][0] - 1 - g)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if which == 0 and x < 0.0 then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# sinh x = x (1 + x^2/6 + ...) rounds to x for |x| < 2^-27
pub fn sinh(x: f64) -> f64
if fabs(x) < 7.450580596923828e-09
return x
return sinh_cosh(x, 0)

# cosh x = 1 + x^2/2 + ... rounds to 1 for |x| < 2^-27
pub fn cosh(x: f64) -> f64
if fabs(x) < 7.450580596923828e-09
return 1.0
return sinh_cosh(x, 1)

# tanh x = x (1 - x^2/3 + ...) rounds to x for |x| < 2^-27, and
# 1 - tanh x < 2 e^(-2|x|) < 2^-60 for |x| > 22 rounds to 1
pub fn tanh(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax < 7.450580596923828e-09
return x
if ax > 22.0
return if x < 0.0 then -1.0 else 1.0
let ex = hyp_ex(ax)
for f in ZIV_F
let fe = f + ex
let h = hyp_parts(ax, fe + 64)
let t = n_div(&h[1], &h[2], fe)
let z = ziv(&t, 0 - fe)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if x < 0.0 then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0


# ---- asinh, acosh, atanh ----------------------------------------------------
# All three are logs of a value U / 2^G >= 1 known to about one unit:
# log = e ln2 + 2 atanh((u - 1)/(u + 1)) with u = U 2^-(G + e) in [0.75, 1.5).

# log(U 2^-G) = (neg ? -1 : 1) N 2^-fo for U > 0 (fo <= 4200): [[neg], N]
fn log_fixed(u: &[i64], gg: i64, fo: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let b = n_bits(u)
var e = b - 1 - gg
# top bits: u / 2^(b-1) >= 1.5 means the next power of two
# (u = 1, b = 1: the top bits are 10)
let t2 = if b >= 2 then n_shr(u, b - 2) else n_shl(u, 1)
if n_to_i64(&t2) == 3
e += 1
let p = n_pow2(gg + e)
let neg = n_cmp(u, &p) < 0
let num = if neg then n_sub(&p, u) else n_sub(u, &p)
let den = n_add(u, &p)
let z = n_div(&num, &den, fo)
let lm = atanh2_fix(&z, fo)
let c = c_ln2x()
let l = cst(&c, 4200, fo)
let el = n_muls(&l, if e < 0 then 0 - e else e)
# e ln2 + (neg ? -lm : lm)
let a_neg = e < 0
if a_neg == neg
return [[if neg then 1 else 0], n_add(&el, &lm)]
if n_cmp(&el, &lm) >= 0
return [[if a_neg then 1 else 0], n_sub(&el, &lm)]
return [[if neg then 1 else 0], n_sub(&lm, &el)]

# x + sqrt(x^2 +- 1) = 2^t (x' + sqrt(x'^2 +- 2^-2t)) with x' = x 2^-t <= 1
# (t = max(0, E + 53) for x = M 2^E), as U / 2^(G - t): [U, G - t]; the
# 2^-2t term is truncated at 2^-2G (one unit of the square root at most)
fn hyp_u(x: f64, gg: i64, sgn: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let m = mant_any(x)
let t = if m[1] + 53 > 0 then m[1] + 53 else 0
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let sx = m[1] - t + gg
let xg = if sx >= 0 then n_shl(&mm, sx) else n_shr(&mm, 0 - sx)
let m2 = n_mul(&mm, &mm)
let a = if sx >= 0 then n_shl(&m2, 2 * sx) else n_shr(&m2, 0 - 2 * sx)
let one = if 2 * gg - 2 * t >= 0 then n_pow2(2 * gg - 2 * t) else []
let s2 = if sgn > 0 then n_add(&a, &one) else n_sub(&a, &one)
let s = n_isqrt(&s2)
return [n_add(&xg, &s), [gg - t]]

# asinh x = x (1 - x^2/6 + ...) rounds to x for |x| < 2^-27
pub fn asinh(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax < 7.450580596923828e-09
return x
let ex = hyp_ex(ax)
for f in ZIV_F
let gg = f + ex + 64
let u = hyp_u(ax, gg, 1)
let r = log_fixed(&u[0], u[1][0], gg)
let z = ziv(&r[1], 0 - gg)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if x < 0.0 then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# acosh x = log(x + sqrt(x^2 - 1)) for x >= 1 (x < 1 traps); the result is
# at least acosh(1 + 2^-52) > 2^-26, so G = f + 96 covers the cancellation
pub fn acosh(x: f64) -> f64
if x < 1.0
return 0.0 / 0.0
if x == 1.0
return 0.0
for f in ZIV_F
let gg = f + 96
let u = hyp_u(x, gg, -1)
let r = log_fixed(&u[0], u[1][0], gg)
let z = ziv(&r[1], 0 - gg)
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# atanh x = log((1 + |x|) / (1 - |x|)) / 2, |x| = M 2^E: the ratio is
# (2^-E + M) / (2^-E - M); rounds to x for |x| < 2^-27; |x| >= 1 traps
pub fn atanh(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax >= 1.0
return 0.0 / 0.0
if ax < 7.450580596923828e-09
return x
let ex = hyp_ex(ax)
let m = mant(ax)
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let p = n_pow2(0 - m[1])
let a = n_add(&p, &mm)
let b = n_sub(&p, &mm)
for f in ZIV_F
let gg = f + ex + 64
let u = n_div(&a, &b, gg)
let r = log_fixed(&u, gg, gg)
let z = ziv(&r[1], 0 - gg - 1)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if x < 0.0 then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0


# ---- expm1, log1p ---------------------------------------------------------
# expm1 x = N 2^(k - g) - 1 from exp_big, at g = f + ex + 64 fraction bits
# (ex ~ log2(1 / |x|) bits cancel); x + x^2/2 rounds to x for |x| < 2^-54,
# and e^x < 2^-54 rounds -1 + e^x to -1 for x < -38
pub fn expm1(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax < 5.551115123125783e-17
return x
if x > 709.7827128933841
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
if x < -38.0
return -1.0
let ex = hyp_ex(ax)
for f in ZIV_F
let g = f + ex + 64
let xf = fix(ax, g)
let p = exp_big(x < 0.0, &xf, g)
let k = p[0][0]
let one = n_pow2(g)
let v = if k >= 0 then n_shl(&p[1], k) else n_shr(&p[1], 0 - k)
let neg = n_cmp(&v, &one) < 0
let d = if neg then n_sub(&one, &v) else n_sub(&v, &one)
let z = ziv(&d, 0 - g)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if neg then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# log1p x = log(U 2^-(G - t)) with U = 2^(G - t) + M 2^(E + G - t) exact
# (x = M 2^E, t = max(0, E + 53) keeps U near G bits; for t > G the 1 is
# below a unit and dropped); x - x^2/2 rounds to x for |x| < 2^-54;
# x <= -1 traps
pub fn log1p(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if x <= -1.0
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
if ax < 5.551115123125783e-17
return x
let ex = hyp_ex(ax)
let m = mant_any(ax)
let t = if m[1] + 53 > 0 then m[1] + 53 else 0
let mm = n_of(m[0])
for f in ZIV_F
let g = f + ex + 64
let gt = g - t
let one = if gt >= 0 then n_pow2(gt) else []
let xg = n_shl(&mm, m[1] + gt)
let u = if x < 0.0 then n_sub(&one, &xg) else n_add(&one, &xg)
let r = log_fixed(&u, gt, g)
let z = ziv(&r[1], 0 - g)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if r[0][0] == 1 then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# ---- exp2, exp10 ----------------------------------------------------------
# exp2: x = k + r, 0 <= r < 1, 2^x = exp(r ln2) 2^k; an integer x is exact
# (2^-1075 is a midpoint, n_round ties it to even). For other rational x,
# 2^x is irrational, so Ziv terminates. 1 + x ln2 rounds to 1 for
# |x| < 2^-55.
pub fn exp2(x: f64) -> f64
if x >= 1024.0
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
if x < -1080.0
return 0.0
if fabs(x) < 2.7755575615628914e-17
return 1.0
let k = x.floor()
let ki = k as i64
let one = [1]
if k == x
return n_round(&one, ki)
for f in ZIV_F
# r = x - k exactly (x - k in binary64 is inexact for tiny x < 0)
let xf = fix(x, f)
let kf = n_pow2(f)
let kk = n_muls(&kf, if ki < 0 then 0 - ki else ki)
let rf = if x < 0.0 then n_sub(&kk, &xf) else n_sub(&xf, &kk)
let c = c_ln2()
let l = cst(&c, 2100, f)
let rl = n_mul(&rf, &l)
let r = n_shr(&rl, f)
let e = exp_fix(&r, f)
let z = ziv(&e, ki - f)
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# exp10 x = exp(x ln10); integer 0 <= x <= 308 exact as 5^x 2^x (10^23 is a
# midpoint), other x give irrational (or, for negative integers,
# non-dyadic) results, so no midpoints; 1 + x ln10 rounds to 1 for
# |x| < 2^-57
pub fn exp10(x: f64) -> f64
if x > 308.3
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
if x < -330.0
return 0.0
if fabs(x) < 6.938893903907228e-18
return 1.0
if x == x.floor() and x > 0.0
let n = x as i64
let five = [5]
let p = n_pow(&five, n)
return n_round(&p, n)
let ax = fabs(x)
for f in ZIV_F
let xf = fix(ax, f + 16)
let c = c_ln10()
let l = cst(&c, 2100, f + 16)
let zl = n_mul(&xf, &l)
let z0 = n_shr(&zl, f + 16)
let p = exp_big(x < 0.0, &z0, f + 16)
let z = ziv(&p[1], p[0][0] - f - 16)
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0


# ---- sinpi, cospi, tanpi ----------------------------------------------------
# |x| = M 2^E with E < 0: 2|x| = k + 2r exactly (k = M >> (-E - 1), r =
# R 2^E in [0, 1/2)); r > 1/4 folds to 1/2 - r with sin and cos swapped.
# theta = pi r at F = f + ex + 8 fraction bits (2^-ex ~ r, so F <= 3200 and
# the 4200-bit pi suffices), off by under one unit. The results are
# irrational except 0, +-1/2, +-1 (Niven), all representable, so no midpoint
# stalls Ziv. which: 0 sinpi, 1 cospi, 2 tanpi.
fn trigpi(x: f64, which: i64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
let sg = x < 0.0 and which != 1
if ax >= 4503599627370496.0
# an integer: sin, tan = 0, cos = (-1)^x
if which == 1
let h = ax * 0.5
return if h == h.floor() then 1.0 else -1.0
return if sg then 0.0 * (0.0 - 1.0) else 0.0
let m = mant_any(ax)
let mm = n_of(m[0])
if m[1] >= 0
if which == 1
let h = ax * 0.5
return if h == h.floor() then 1.0 else -1.0
return if sg then 0.0 * (0.0 - 1.0) else 0.0
let fx = 0 - m[1]
let kn = n_shr(&mm, fx - 1)
let q = n_to_i64(&kn) % 4
# fx = 1: x is a half-integer, r = 0
var rn = if fx >= 2 then n_low(&mm, fx - 1) else []
let quarter = if fx >= 2 then n_pow2(fx - 2) else []
var sw = false
if fx >= 2 and n_cmp(&rn, &quarter) > 0
let half = n_pow2(fx - 1)
rn = n_sub(&half, &rn)
sw = true
# sin(pi(q/2 + r)) = [S, C, -S, -C][q], cos = [C, -S, -C, S][q]
let s_is_s = q % 2 == 0
let s_neg = q >= 2
let c_neg = q == 1 or q == 2
if rn.len() == 0
# r = 0: S = 0, C = 1 (swap makes it r = 1/2, but then rn was > 1/4)
let sv = if s_is_s then 0.0 else (if s_neg then -1.0 else 1.0)
let cv = if s_is_s then (if c_neg then -1.0 else 1.0) else 0.0
var v = if which == 0 then sv else cv
if which == 2
v = sv / cv
if which == 2 and sv == 0.0
v = if s_neg != c_neg then 0.0 * (0.0 - 1.0) else 0.0
return if sg then chs(v) else v
let ex = fx - n_bits(&rn)
for f in ZIV_F
let ff = f + ex + 8
let c = c_pi()
let pf = cst(&c, 4200, ff)
let tp = n_mul(&rn, &pf)
let th = n_shr(&tp, fx)
let sc = sincos_fix(&th, ff)
# S, C of r from sin, cos of theta (swapped when folded)
let cfirst = s_is_s == sw
let sv = if cfirst then n_shr(&sc[1], 0) else n_shr(&sc[0], 0)
let cv = if cfirst then n_shr(&sc[0], 0) else n_shr(&sc[1], 0)
var v: List[i64] = []
var neg = false
if which == 0
v = sv
neg = s_neg
elif which == 1
v = cv
neg = c_neg
else
v = n_div(&sv, &cv, ff)
neg = s_neg != c_neg
let z = ziv(&v, 0 - ff)
if z[0] == z[1]
let r = if neg != sg then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return r
return 0.0 / 0.0

pub fn sinpi(x: f64) -> f64
return trigpi(x, 0)

pub fn cospi(x: f64) -> f64
return trigpi(x, 1)

# tanpi of a half-integer is a pole and traps
pub fn tanpi(x: f64) -> f64
return trigpi(x, 2)


# ---- erf, erfc ------------------------------------------------------------
# erf x = (2/sqrt(pi)) e^(-x^2) sum_n 2^n x^(2n+1) / (1 3 ... (2n+1)), all
# terms positive. erf_fix gives erf |x| 2^G (G <= 4200; each of the n
# terms is off by under a unit, n < 4 x^2 + G, and e^(-x^2) shrinks the
# sum's error: well inside Ziv's 2^16 units for x <= 27.3).
fn erf_fix(ax: f64, gg: i64) -> List[i64]
let m = mant_any(ax)
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let m2 = n_mul(&mm, &mm)
let sx = 2 * m[1] + gg
let x2 = if sx >= 0 then n_shl(&m2, sx) else n_shr(&m2, 0 - sx)
let xs = m[1] + gg
var t = if xs >= 0 then n_shl(&mm, xs) else n_shr(&mm, 0 - xs)
var s = n_shr(&t, 0)
var n: i64 = 0
# t 2x^2 = (t 2 M^2) 2^(2E): a short multiplier, not the G-bit x^2
let m22 = n_muls(&m2, 2)
while t.len() > 0 bound 1048576
n += 1
let p = n_mul(&t, &m22)
let ps = if 2 * m[1] <= 0 then n_shr(&p, 0 - 2 * m[1]) else n_shl(&p, 2 * m[1])
t = n_divs(&ps, 2 * n + 1)
s = n_add(&s, &t)
let e = exp_big(true, &x2, gg)
let c = c_2osqrtpi()
let cg = cst(&c, 4200, gg)
let es = n_mul(&e[1], &s)
let p = n_mul(&es, &cg)
# erf = p 2^(k - 3G) (e is 2^(k - G) N), so erf 2^G = p >> (2G - k)
return n_shr(&p, 2 * gg - e[0][0])

# erf x = 2x/sqrt(pi) (1 - x^2/3 + ...): G = f + ex + 64 keeps relative
# precision for tiny x (ex ~ log2(1/|x|)); 1 - erf x = erfc x < 2^-54 rounds
# to 1 for |x| >= 6
pub fn erf(x: f64) -> f64
let ax = fabs(x)
if ax == 0.0
return x
if ax >= 6.0
return if x < 0.0 then -1.0 else 1.0
let ex = hyp_ex(ax)
for f in ZIV_F
let gg = f + ex + 64
let v = erf_fix(ax, gg)
let z = ziv(&v, 0 - gg)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if x < 0.0 then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0

# erfc x = e^(-x^2) / (x sqrt(pi)) sum_n (-1)^n (2n-1)!! / (2x^2)^n for large
# x: the series is asymptotic but alternating with the remainder below the
# first omitted term, and its terms fall below 2^-G (G bits) well before
# they turn around once 1.44 x^2 > G; when they turn first the sum stops
# at the smallest term (the remainder is below it: about 2^-(1.44 x^2)
# relative, so for x > 9 still far below a double's worst cases).
# [[sh], W, B]: erfc x = W 2^sh with W of G bits, off by under B units.
fn erfc_asym(x: f64, gg: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let m = mant(x)
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let m2 = n_mul(&mm, &mm)
# 1 / (2 x^2) = 2^(-2E - 1) / M^2 at 2G fraction bits
let one = n_pow2(2 * gg - 2 * m[1] - 1)
let inv = n_div(&one, &m2, 0)
var t = n_pow2(gg)
var pos = n_pow2(gg)
var neg: List[i64] = []
var n: i64 = 0
var ok = false
var err: List[i64] = []
while not ok bound 100000
n += 1
let tm = n_muls(&t, 2 * n - 1)
let p = n_mul(&tm, &inv)
let t2 = n_shr(&p, 2 * gg)
if t2.len() == 0
ok = true
elif n_cmp(&t2, &t) >= 0
# the terms turn: stop, the remainder is below t
ok = true
err = n_shr(&t, 0)
else
if n % 2 == 1
neg = n_add(&neg, &t2)
else
pos = n_add(&pos, &t2)
t = t2
let a = n_sub(&pos, &neg)
let xf = fix(x, gg)
let x2f = n_mul(&xf, &xf)
let x2 = n_shr(&x2f, gg)
let e = exp_big(true, &x2, gg)
let c = c_2osqrtpi()
let cg = cst(&c, 4200, gg)
let ec = n_mul(&e[1], &cg)
let eca = n_mul(&ec, &a)
# erfc = eca 2^(k - 3G - 1) / x, x = M 2^E
let w = n_div(&eca, &mm, 0)
let drop = n_bits(&w) - gg
let wd = n_shr(&w, drop)
# the remainder (t units of 2^-G, the sum A is about 2^G) is under
# 2 t + 2 units of W's G bits: the Ziv bound EB + 2 t + 2
let ebn = n_of(EB + 2)
let e2 = n_muls(&err, 2)
return [[e[0][0] - 3 * gg - 1 - m[1] + drop], wd, n_add(&ebn, &e2)]

# erfc x = 1 - erf x: for x > 0 about 1.45 x^2 bits cancel (erfc x ~
# e^(-x^2) / (x sqrt(pi))), so G = f + 72 + 1.45 x^2 (<= 3200); erfc x
# underflows to 0 past 27.3, and is 2 - erfc|x| (rounds to 2) for x <= -6
pub fn erfc(x: f64) -> f64
if x == 0.0
return 1.0
if x > 27.3
return 0.0
if x <= -6.0
return 2.0
let ax = fabs(x)
let ex = hyp_ex(ax)
let lose = (1.45 * x * x) as i64
for f in ZIV_F
if x > 0.0 and lose > 120
let r = erfc_asym(x, f + 64)
let z = ziv_eb(&r[1], r[0][0], &r[2])
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
let gg = f + 72 + ex + (if x > 0.0 then lose else 0)
let v = erf_fix(ax, gg)
let one = n_pow2(gg)
let d = if x > 0.0 then n_sub(&one, &v) else n_add(&one, &v)
let z = ziv(&d, 0 - gg)
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
return 0.0 / 0.0


# ---- tgamma, lgamma ---------------------------------------------------------
# Kummer: for x = X / 2^s >= 1 and an integer N > x - 1,
# Gamma(x) = e^(x log N - N) S + Gamma(x, N), S = sum_k N^k / (x (x+1) ... (x+k))
# (all terms positive), and Gamma(x, N) <= N^(x-1) e^-N / (1 - (x-1)/N).
# N is chosen (in binary64, with the Stirling lower bound
# lgamma x > (x - 1/2) log x - x + 0.9189) so that the omitted tail is
# below 2^-(G+8) of Gamma(x). Each term is off by under a unit at G + 16
# fraction bits and S >= 1/x, so S keeps G bits.
# [[vneg, g2], v, S]: v / 2^g2 = x log N - N (vneg: negative), S / 2^(G+16).
fn kummer(xn: &[i64], s: i64, gg: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let xd = n_round(xn, 0 - s)
let lgl = (xd - 0.5) * log_d(xd) - xd + 0.9189
var nn = ((xd + 0.7 * (gg as f64)) as i64) + 16
var go = true
while go bound 100000
let nd = nn as f64
let tl = (xd - 1.0) * log_d(nd) - nd - log_d(1.0 - (xd - 1.0) / nd) - lgl
if tl < 0.0 - ((gg + 8) as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
go = false
else
nn += 8
let g1 = gg + 16
let one = n_pow2(g1)
var t = n_div(&one, xn, s)
var sum = n_shr(&t, 0)
var k: i64 = 0
let ks = n_pow2(s)
var den = n_shr(xn, 0)
var fin = false
while not fin bound 1048576
k += 1
den = n_add(&den, &ks)
let tn = n_muls(&t, nn)
t = n_div(&tn, &den, s)
sum = n_add(&sum, &t)
# x + k > 2N: the rest is below t (1 + 1/2 + ...) = 2t < 2 units
if t.len() == 0 and xd + (k as f64) > 2.0 * (nn as f64)
fin = true
let g2 = gg + 32
let nb = n_of(nn)
let ln = log_fixed(&nb, 0, g2)
let xl = n_mul(xn, &ln[1])
let xls = n_shr(&xl, s)
let nf = n_shl(&nb, g2)
let vneg = n_cmp(&xls, &nf) < 0
let v = if vneg then n_sub(&nf, &xls) else n_sub(&xls, &nf)
return [[if vneg then 1 else 0, g2], v, sum]

# natural log of a binary64 > 0, to binary64 accuracy (for choosing N only)
fn log_d(x: f64) -> f64
let fr = frexp1(x)
let m = fr[0]
# log m for m in [0.5, 1): 2 atanh((m-1)/(m+1)), enough terms
let z = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
let z2 = z * z
var s = 0.0
var t = z
for i in 0..40
s = s + t / ((2 * i + 1) as f64)
t = t * z2
return 2.0 * s + fr[1] * 0.6931471805599453

# Gamma(x) for x = X / 2^s >= 1: [[sh], P], Gamma = P 2^sh to G bits
# (exp of lgamma_pos, which is good to 2^-G absolute; lgamma < 2^10 here)
fn gamma_big(xn: &[i64], s: i64, x: f64, gg: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let l = lgamma_pos(xn, s, x, gg + 12)
let e = exp_big(l[0][0] == 1, &l[1], gg + 12)
return [[e[0][0] - gg - 12], n_shr(&e[1], 0)]

# log Gamma(x) for x = X / 2^s >= 1 at G fraction bits: [[neg], L]
fn lgamma_kummer(xn: &[i64], s: i64, gg: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let kp = kummer(xn, s, gg)
let ls = log_fixed(&kp[2], gg + 16, gg + 16)
let v = n_shr(&kp[1], kp[0][1] - gg - 16)
let r = sadd(kp[0][0] == 1, &v, ls[0][0] == 1, &ls[1])
return [[r[0][0]], n_shr(&r[1], 16)]

# signed add: (an ? -a : a) + (bn ? -b : b) as [[neg], |sum|]
fn sadd(an: bool, a: &[i64], bn: bool, b: &[i64]) -> List[List[i64]]
if an == bn
return [[if an then 1 else 0], n_add(a, b)]
if n_cmp(a, b) >= 0
return [[if an then 1 else 0], n_sub(a, b)]
return [[if bn then 1 else 0], n_sub(b, a)]

# Stirling for x = X / 2^s: lgamma x = (x - 1/2) log x - x + log(2 pi)/2
# + sum_{k=1..20} B_2k / (2k (2k-1) x^(2k-1)), the remainder below the next
# term (alternating) and below 2^-(G+8) once x >= 2^((G + 54) / 42).
# G fraction bits (G <= 4100): L > 0.
fn lgamma_stirling(xn: &[i64], s: i64, gg: i64) -> List[i64]
let g = gg + 16
let lx = log_fixed(xn, s, g)
let xf = if g >= s then n_shl(xn, g - s) else n_shr(xn, s - g)
let hf = n_pow2(g - 1)
let xh = n_sub(&xf, &hf)
let a = n_mul(&xh, &lx[1])
let a1 = n_shr(&a, g)
let c = c_hl2pi()
let hc = cst(&c, 4200, g)
let b = n_add(&a1, &hc)
var r = n_sub(&b, &xf)
# 1/x and 1/x^2 at g fraction bits
let num = n_pow2(g)
let inv = n_div(&num, xn, s)
let i2p = n_mul(&inv, &inv)
let inv2 = n_shr(&i2p, g)
var p = n_shr(&inv, 0)
var pos: List[i64] = []
var neg: List[i64] = []
for k in 0..20
let csk = c_stir(k)
let ck = cst(&csk, 4200, g)
let tp = n_mul(&ck, &p)
let t = n_shr(&tp, g)
if k % 2 == 0
pos = n_add(&pos, &t)
else
neg = n_add(&neg, &t)
let pp = n_mul(&p, &inv2)
p = n_shr(&pp, g)
r = n_add(&r, &pos)
r = n_sub(&r, &neg)
return n_shr(&r, 16)

# Stirling's threshold 2^((G + 54) / 42), rounded up
fn stir_min(gg: i64) -> f64
return pow2((gg + 54) / 42 + 1)

# log Gamma(x) for x = X / 2^s >= 1 at G fraction bits, [[neg], L]:
# lgamma(x + n) - log(x (x+1) ... (x+n-1)) with x + n past Stirling's
# threshold (the product kept to G + 64 bits: n roundings of 2^-(G+64)),
# else (n > 4096, only for G > 300) Kummer
fn lgamma_pos(xn: &[i64], s: i64, x: f64, gg: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let ym = stir_min(gg)
if x >= ym
return [[0], lgamma_stirling(xn, s, gg)]
let n = (ym - x).floor() as i64 + 1
if n > 4096
return lgamma_kummer(xn, s, gg)
let ks = n_pow2(s)
var d = n_shr(xn, 0)
var pr = [1]
var pe: i64 = 0
for _j in 0..n
pr = n_mul(&pr, &d)
d = n_add(&d, &ks)
let ex = n_bits(&pr) - gg - 64
if ex > 0
pr = n_shr(&pr, ex)
pe += ex
let ls = lgamma_stirling(&d, s, gg)
let lp = log_fixed(&pr, s * n - pe, gg)
return sadd(false, &ls, lp[0][0] == 0, &lp[1])

# W 2^sh to f + 40 significant bits for Ziv (P is good to G = f + 64 bits)
fn ziv_rel(p: &[i64], sh: i64, f: i64) -> List[f64]
let drop = n_bits(p) - f - 40
let w = if drop >= 0 then n_shr(p, drop) else n_shl(p, 0 - drop)
return ziv(&w, sh + drop)

# |sin(pi x)| for x = M 2^E > 0 not an integer: [[ff], V], V 2^-ff, with
# G significant bits: d = distance to the nearest integer, sin(pi d) or
# cos(pi (1/2 - d)) when d > 1/4
fn sinpi_abs(x: f64, gg: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let m = mant_any(x)
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let fx = 0 - m[1]
if fx == 1
return [[gg], n_pow2(gg)]
let r1 = n_low(&mm, fx)
let one = n_pow2(fx)
let r2 = n_sub(&one, &r1)
let d = if n_cmp(&r1, &r2) <= 0 then r1 else r2
let quarter = n_pow2(fx - 2)
let half = n_pow2(fx - 1)
let sw = n_cmp(&d, &quarter) > 0
let rn = if sw then n_sub(&half, &d) else d
let ex = if rn.len() == 0 then 0 else fx - n_bits(&rn)
let ff = gg + ex + 8
let c = c_pi()
let pf = cst(&c, 4200, ff)
let tp = n_mul(&rn, &pf)
let th = n_shr(&tp, fx)
let sc = sincos_fix(&th, ff)
return [[ff], if sw then n_shr(&sc[1], 0) else n_shr(&sc[0], 0)]

# x as X / 2^s exactly (x > 0): [X, [s]]
fn as_frac(x: f64) -> List[List[i64]]
let m = mant_any(x)
let mm = n_of(m[0])
if m[1] >= 0
return [n_shl(&mm, m[1]), [0]]
return [mm, [0 - m[1]]]

# Gamma and lgamma for tiny x = M 2^E (|x| < 2^-ex): Gamma(x) =
# (1 - g x + c2 x^2 + O(x^3)) / x with g Euler's constant and c2 = g^2/2 +
# pi^2/12 (|c3| < 0.91), lgamma x = -log |x| - g x + c2 x^2 + O(x^3). When
# 3 ex >= G + 2 the dropped terms are under a unit of 2^-G, so this replaces
# the product loop, Stirling and exp for |x| < 2^-((G + 2) / 3).
fn tiny_ok(x: f64, gg: i64) -> bool
return 3 * hyp_ex(fabs(x)) >= gg + 2

# 1 - g x + c2 x^2 at G fraction bits (|x| < 2^-30, so W > 0)
fn tiny_w(x: f64, gg: i64) -> List[i64]
let m = mant_any(fabs(x))
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let cg = c_euler()
let g1 = cst(&cg, 2100, gg)
let gm = n_mul(&g1, &mm)
let gx = n_shr(&gm, 0 - m[1])
let cc = c_g2()
let c1 = cst(&cc, 2100, gg)
let m2 = n_mul(&mm, &mm)
let cm = n_mul(&c1, &m2)
let cx = n_shr(&cm, 0 - 2 * m[1])
let one = n_pow2(gg)
let w = n_add(&one, &cx)
return if x > 0.0 then n_sub(&w, &gx) else n_add(&w, &gx)

fn tgamma_tiny(x: f64, f: i64, gg: i64) -> List[f64]
let m = mant_any(fabs(x))
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let w = tiny_w(x, gg)
let q = n_div(&w, &mm, 64)
let z = ziv_rel(&q, 0 - 64 - gg - m[1], f)
return if x < 0.0 then [chs(z[1]), chs(z[0])] else z

# -log |x| - g x + c2 x^2 = -log |x| + (W - 1)
fn lgamma_tiny(x: f64, gg: i64) -> List[f64]
let m = mant_any(fabs(x))
let mm = n_of(m[0])
let lx = log_fixed(&mm, 0 - m[1], gg)
let w = tiny_w(x, gg)
let one = n_pow2(gg)
let wneg = n_cmp(&w, &one) < 0
let d = if wneg then n_sub(&one, &w) else n_sub(&w, &one)
let r = sadd(lx[0][0] == 0, &lx[1], wneg, &d)
let z = ziv(&r[1], 0 - gg)
return if r[0][0] == 1 then [chs(z[1]), chs(z[0])] else z

# 1 + |x| as X / 2^s, cut to t fraction bits when s > t: Gamma and lgamma
# have slope under 1 on [1, 2], so for tiny |x| the cut moves Gamma(1 + |x|)
# by under 2^-t, and the product loop and Stirling then work on t-bit
# numbers instead of s-bit ones (s reaches 1126 for subnormal x)
fn one_plus(xn: &[i64], s: i64, t: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let ones = n_pow2(s)
let x1 = n_add(xn, &ones)
if s > t
return [n_shr(&x1, s - t), [t]]
return [x1, [s]]

# tgamma: positive integers n <= 171 are exact ((n-1)!, rounded once);
# 0 and negative integers are poles (trap); x >= 1 by Kummer; 0 < x < 1 as
# Gamma(1 + x) / x; x < 0 by reflection pi / (sin(pi x) Gamma(1 - x)),
# and |Gamma(x)| < 2^45 / Gamma(191) < 2^-1075 for x < -190. Overflow past
# 171.62 traps.
pub fn tgamma(x: f64) -> f64
if x > 171.7
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
if x == x.floor()
if x <= 0.0
return 0.0 / 0.0
var p = [1]
let n = x as i64
for i in 1..n
p = n_muls(&p, i)
return n_round(&p, 0)
if x < -190.0
# sign of Gamma(x) for x < 0: (-1)^ceil(-x)
let c = (0.0 - x).floor() + 1.0
let h = c * 0.5
return if h == h.floor() then 0.0 else 0.0 * (0.0 - 1.0)
let ax = fabs(x)
let fr = as_frac(ax)
let s = fr[1][0]
let _ones = n_pow2(s)
for f in ZIV_F
let gg = f + 64
if tiny_ok(x, gg)
let zt = tgamma_tiny(x, f, gg)
if zt[0] == zt[1]
return zt[0]
elif x >= 1.0
let g = gamma_big(&fr[0], s, x, gg)
let z = ziv_rel(&g[1], g[0][0], f)
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
elif x > 0.0
let o = one_plus(&fr[0], s, gg + 16)
let g = gamma_big(&o[0], o[1][0], 1.0 + ax, gg)
let q = n_div(&g[1], &fr[0], s + 64)
let z = ziv_rel(&q, g[0][0] - 64, f)
if z[0] == z[1]
return z[0]
else
let o = one_plus(&fr[0], s, gg + 16)
let g = gamma_big(&o[0], o[1][0], 1.0 + ax, gg)
let sp = sinpi_abs(ax, gg)
let den = n_mul(&sp[1], &g[1])
let c = c_pi()
let pg = cst(&c, 4200, gg)
# pi 2^-G / (V 2^-ff P 2^sh)
let dbits = n_bits(&den)
let q = n_div(&pg, &den, dbits + 64)
let z = ziv_rel(&q, 0 - gg + sp[0][0] - g[0][0] - dbits - 64, f)
if z[0] == z[1]
# Gamma(x) < 0 when ceil(-x) is odd
let c1 = ax.floor() + 1.0
let h = c1 * 0.5
return if h == h.floor() then z[0] else chs(z[0])
return 0.0 / 0.0

# lgamma x = log |Gamma(x)|: 0 at 1 and 2 (exact); poles (0, negative
# integers) trap; 0 < x < 1 as lgamma(1 + x) - log x; x < 0 as
# log pi - log |sin(pi x)| - lgamma(1 - x). Near the zeros of lgamma bits
# cancel: G grows by the shortfall and the step repeats (G <= 4200).
# log |Gamma(x)| at G fraction bits for non-tiny x = X / 2^s, [[neg], L]
fn lgamma_at(x: f64, xn: &[i64], s: i64, gg: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let ax = fabs(x)
if x >= 1.0
return lgamma_pos(xn, s, x, gg)
let o = one_plus(xn, s, gg + 16)
if x > 0.0
let a = lgamma_pos(&o[0], o[1][0], x + 1.0, gg)
let lx = log_fixed(xn, s, gg)
return sadd(a[0][0] == 1, &a[1], lx[0][0] == 0, &lx[1])
let a = lgamma_pos(&o[0], o[1][0], 1.0 - x, gg)
let sp = sinpi_abs(ax, gg)
# log(pi / |sin|) = log(pi 2^ff / V)
let c = c_pi()
let pg = cst(&c, 4200, gg + 8)
let q = n_div(&pg, &sp[1], sp[0][0] - 8)
let lq = log_fixed(&q, gg, gg)
return sadd(lq[0][0] == 1, &lq[1], a[0][0] == 0, &a[1])

pub fn lgamma(x: f64) -> f64
if x == 1.0 or x == 2.0
return 0.0
if x <= 0.0 and x == x.floor()
return 0.0 / 0.0
if x > 2.5599833278516383e305
return 1.7976931348623157e308 * 2.0
let fr = as_frac(fabs(x))
let s = fr[1][0]
# below 3 lgamma has its zeros (1, 2 and one in each (-n-1, -n)): a
# 96-bit probe (cheap: Stirling from 16 on) gives log2(1 / |lgamma x|),
# so the first full step already carries the bits that cancel
var lost: i64 = 0
if x < 3.0 and not tiny_ok(x, 96)
let r0 = lgamma_at(x, &fr[0], s, 96)
lost = 96 - n_bits(&r0[1]) - 24
if lost < 0 or lost > 1000
lost = 0
for f in ZIV_F
var gg = f + 64 + (if lost > 0 then lost + 8 else 0)
if tiny_ok(x, f + 64)
let zt = lgamma_tiny(x, f + 64)
if zt[0] == zt[1]
return zt[0]
var tries: i64 = 0
while tries < 4 bound 4
tries += 1
let r = lgamma_at(x, &fr[0], s, gg)
let short = f + 40 - n_bits(&r[1])
if short > 0 and gg + short <= 4100 and tries < 4
gg = gg + short + 8
else
let z = ziv(&r[1], 0 - gg)
if z[0] == z[1]
return if r[0][0] == 1 then chs(z[0]) else z[0]
tries = 4
return 0.0 / 0.0


# ---- pow ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Exact and midpoint results happen only for integer y (odd part of x to
# the y-th power at most 54 bits) and for y = n / 2^k, k <= 5, with x's odd
# part a perfect 2^k-th power: those are computed exactly and rounded once
# (ties to even). Every other x^y is neither, and is exp(y log x) with
# Ziv's loop (log at enough extra bits that y log x is known to 2^-f).

fn chs(v: f64) -> f64
return v * (0.0 - 1.0)

# [[neg], N]: log x = (neg ? -1 : 1) N / 2^fe, x > 0
fn log_big(x: f64, fe: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let fr = frexp1(x)
var m = fr[0]
var e = fr[1] as i64
if m >= 1.5
m = m * 0.5
e += 1
let mm = (m * P52 * 2.0) as i64
let one: i64 = 9007199254740992
let neg = mm < one
let num = if neg then one - mm else mm - one
let den = mm + one
let lm = if num == 0 then [] else log_fix(num, den, fe)
let c = c_ln2()
let l = cst(&c, 2100, fe)
let el = n_muls(&l, if e < 0 then 0 - e else e)
let a_neg = e < 0
if a_neg == neg
return [[if neg then 1 else 0], n_add(&el, &lm)]
if n_cmp(&el, &lm) >= 0
return [[if a_neg then 1 else 0], n_sub(&el, &lm)]
return [[if neg then 1 else 0], n_sub(&lm, &el)]

# [[k], N]: exp(v) = N 2^(k - f) for v = (zneg ? -1 : 1) z / 2^f, |v| < 2048
# (f <= 4200)
fn exp_big(zneg: bool, z: &[i64], f: i64) -> List[List[i64]]
let zd = n_round(z, 0 - f)
let v = if zneg then 0.0 - zd else zd
var k = (v / 0.6931471805599453).floor() as i64
let c = c_ln2x()
let l = cst(&c, 4200, f)
var r: List[i64] = []
var ok = false
while not ok bound 8
# r = v - k ln2, kept as a magnitude with its sign
let kl = n_muls(&l, if k < 0 then 0 - k else k)
let kneg = k < 0
var rneg = false
if zneg != kneg
r = n_add(z, &kl)
rneg = zneg
elif n_cmp(z, &kl) >= 0
r = n_sub(z, &kl)

module net.dns

# DNS messages (RFC 1035 section 4, survey M25 pure part): encode and
# decode over bytes (List[i64]). Names are text in presentation form
# (RFC 1035 5.1): labels joined by ".", a label byte that is not
# printable ASCII written \DDD, and the specials " $ ( ) . ; @ \ escaped
# with a backslash (as BIND and dnspython write them); the root is ".".
# Decoding follows compression pointers (4.1.4) only backwards, at most 128 of them, and refuses names over 255
# bytes, labels over 63, and the reserved label types 01 and 10. Record
# data of NS, CNAME, PTR, MX, SOA and SRV is returned uncompressed (names
# expanded), so it compares and re-encodes the same; other types are
# kept as bytes. Encoding writes no compression (always valid). No
# resolver here: sending a query is an io request through a host
# adapter (no UDP adapter exists in rce 0.1.3).

error BadDns(why: text)

pub struct Question
name: text
qtype: i64
qclass: i64

pub struct Record
name: text
rtype: i64
rclass: i64
ttl: i64
rdata: List[i64]

pub struct Dns
id: i64
flags: i64
questions: List[Question]
answers: List[Record]
authority: List[Record]
additional: List[Record]

pub const A: i64 = 1
pub const NS: i64 = 2
pub const CNAME: i64 = 5
pub const SOA: i64 = 6
pub const PTR: i64 = 12
pub const MX: i64 = 15
pub const TXT: i64 = 16
pub const AAAA: i64 = 28
pub const SRV: i64 = 33
pub const IN: i64 = 1

const DN_ASCII: text = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~"

fn dch(x: i64) -> text = copy(DN_ASCII.chars()[(x - 32) as usize])

fn d3(x: i64) -> text = (x / 100).tostr() + ((x / 10) % 10).tostr() + (x % 10).tostr()

# ---------------- flags ----------------

pub fn qr(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 15) & 1 == 1
pub fn opcode(f: i64) -> i64 = (f >> 11) & 15
pub fn aa(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 10) & 1 == 1
pub fn tc(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 9) & 1 == 1
pub fn rd(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 8) & 1 == 1
pub fn ra(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 7) & 1 == 1
pub fn rcode(f: i64) -> i64 = f & 15

pub fn make_flags(is_qr: bool, op: i64, is_aa: bool, is_tc: bool, is_rd: bool, is_ra: bool, rc: i64) -> i64
var f = (op & 15) << 11 | (rc & 15)
if is_qr
f = f | 32768
if is_aa
f = f | 1024
if is_tc
f = f | 512
if is_rd
f = f | 256
if is_ra
f = f | 128
return f

# ---------------- names ----------------

# Wire labels of a presentation name (without compression).
pub fn name_wire(n: &text) -> List[i64] ! BadDns
var out: List[i64] = []
if n == "." or n == ""
out.push(0)
return out
let cs = n.chars()
var lab: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 0

# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,

# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)
if c >= S_BASE and c < S_BASE + S_COUNT
let s = c - S_BASE
o.push(L_BASE + s / N_COUNT)
o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)
if s % T_COUNT != 0
o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)
return
let d = decomposition(c)
if d.len() == 0
o.push(c)
return
for x in d
o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
for c in cps
decompose_into(&mut o, c)
var cc: List[i64] = []
for c in o
cc.push(ccc(c))
# stable insertion sort of each run of non-starters by class
var i: usize = 1
while i < o.len() bound 16777216
var j = i
while j > 0 and cc[j] != 0 and cc[j - 1] > cc[j] bound 16777216
let t = o[j]
o[j] = o[j - 1]
o[j - 1] = t
let u = cc[j]
cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
cc[j - 1] = u
j -= 1
i += 1
return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
if a >= L_BASE and a < L_BASE + 19 and b >= V_BASE and b < V_BASE + 21
return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT
if a >= S_BASE and a < S_BASE + S_COUNT and (a - S_BASE) % T_COUNT == 0 and b > T_BASE and b < T_BASE + T_COUNT
return a + (b - T_BASE)
return composite(a * 1114112 + b)

var starter = last == 0
o.push(d[0])
var i: usize = 1
while i < d.len() bound 16777216
let c = d[i]
let cl = ccc(c)
let comp = if starter then compose_pair(o[sp], c) else -1
if starter and (last < cl or last == 0) and comp >= 0
o[sp] = comp
i += 1
continue
if cl == 0
sp = o.len()
starter = true
last = cl
o.push(c)
i += 1
return o

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1
const P_TMAX: i64 = 26
const P_MAX: i64 = 2147483647

fn adapt(delta0: i64, numpoints: i64, first: bool) -> i64
var delta = if first then delta0 / 700 else delta0 / 2
delta += delta / numpoints
var k: i64 = 0
while delta > ((P_BASE - P_TMIN) * P_TMAX) / 2 bound 64
delta = delta / (P_BASE - P_TMIN)
k += P_BASE
return k + (P_BASE - P_TMIN + 1) * delta / (delta + 38)

fn digit_value(c: i64) -> i64
if c >= 48 and c <= 57
return c - 22
if c >= 65 and c <= 90
return c - 65
if c >= 97 and c <= 122
return c - 97
return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
if k <= bias
return P_TMIN
if k >= bias + P_TMAX
return P_TMAX
return k - bias

# Decoding; a failure (bad digit, end inside a number, overflow, a
# result that is not a scalar value) gives err.
pub fn puny_decode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
var o: List[i64] = []
var b: usize = 0
var j: usize = 0
while j < input.len() bound 16777216
if input[j] == 45
b = j
j += 1
var k: usize = 0
while k < b bound 16777216
if input[k] >= 128
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
o.push(input[k])
k += 1
var p: usize = if b > 0 then b + 1 else 0
var n: i64 = 128
var i: i64 = 0
var bias: i64 = 72
while p < input.len() bound 16777216
let oldi = i
var w: i64 = 1
var kk: i64 = P_BASE
loop bound 64
if p >= input.len()
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
let d = digit_value(input[p])
p += 1
if d < 0
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
if d > (P_MAX - i) / w
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
i += d * w
let t = thresh(kk, bias)
if d < t
break
if w > P_MAX / (P_BASE - t)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
w = w * (P_BASE - t)
kk += P_BASE
let len = o.len() as i64 + 1
bias = adapt(i - oldi, len, oldi == 0)
if i / len > P_MAX - n
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
n += i / len
i = i % len
if n > 1114111 or (n >= 55296 and n <= 57343)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
o.push(n)
var q = o.len() - 1
while q > i as usize bound 16777216
o[q] = o[q - 1]
q -= 1
o[i as usize] = n
i += 1
return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
var o: List[i64] = []
for c in input
if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
if c < 128
o.push(c)
let basic = o.len() as i64
var h = basic
if basic > 0
o.push(45)
var n: i64 = 128
var delta: i64 = 0
var bias: i64 = 72
let total = input.len() as i64
while h < total bound 16777216
var m: i64 = P_MAX
for c in input
if c >= n and c < m
m = c
if m - n > (P_MAX - delta) / (h + 1)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
delta += (m - n) * (h + 1)
n = m
for c in input
if c < n
delta += 1
if delta > P_MAX
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
if c == n
var q = delta
var k: i64 = P_BASE
loop bound 64
let t = thresh(k, bias)
if q < t
break
o.push(digit_char(t + (q - t) % (P_BASE - t)))
q = (q - t) / (P_BASE - t)
k += P_BASE
o.push(digit_char(q))
bias = adapt(delta, h + 1, h == basic)
delta = 0
h += 1
delta += 1
n += 1
return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool
for c in l
if c >= 128
return false
return true

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
for c in l
let b = bidi_class(c)
if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
return true
return false

# RFC 5893 section 2, rules 1 to 6, for one label of a bidi domain.
pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
if l.len() == 0
return true
let f = bidi_class(l[0])
if f != 0 and f != 1 and f != 2
return false
var e = l.len()
while e > 0 and bidi_class(l[e - 1]) == 10 bound 16777216
e -= 1
if e == 0
return false
let last = bidi_class(l[e - 1])
if f == 0
for c in l
let b = bidi_class(c)
if b != 0 and b != 4 and b != 5 and b != 6 and b != 7 and b != 8 and b != 9 and b != 10
return false
return last == 0 or last == 4
var en = false
var an = false
for c in l
let b = bidi_class(c)
if b == 0 or b > 10
return false
if b == 4
en = true
if b == 3
an = true
if en and an
return false
return last == 1 or last == 2 or last == 4 or last == 3

# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 (ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER) and A.2 (ZERO WIDTH JOINER).
pub fn joiners_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
var i: usize = 0
while i < l.len() bound 16777216
let c = l[i]
if c == 8204 or c == 8205
let virama = i > 0 and ccc(l[i - 1]) == 9
if not virama
if c == 8205
return false
var a = i
var left = false
while a > 0 bound 16777216
let t = joining_type(l[a - 1])
if t == 5
a -= 1
continue
left = t == 2 or t == 4
break
var z = i + 1
var right = false
while z < l.len() bound 16777216
let t = joining_type(l[z])
if t == 5
z += 1
continue
right = t == 2 or t == 3
break
if not (left and right)
return false
i += 1
return true

# Validity criteria 4.1 except the bidi rules (checked per domain).
fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool
if l.len() == 0
return true
if decoded
let n = nfc(l)
if n != copy(l)
return false
if f.hyphens
if l.len() >= 4 and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45
return false
if l[0] == 45 or l[l.len() - 1] == 45
return false
elif is_xn(l)
return false
if is_mark(l[0])
return false
for c in l
if c == 46
return false
let s = status(c)
if not (s == 0 or (s == 2 and not transitional))
return false
if f.std3 and c < 128 and not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 45)
return false
if f.joiners and not joiners_ok(l)
return false
return true

pub struct Labels

err: bool

# Section 4 processing: the converted labels and the error flag.
pub fn process(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Labels
var m: List[i64] = []
for c in input
let s = status(c)
if s == 4
continue
if s == 1
if f.transitional and c == 7838
m.push(115)
m.push(115)
else
for x in mapping(c)
m.push(x)
elif s == 2 and f.transitional
for x in mapping(c)
m.push(x)
else
m.push(c)
let n = nfc(&m)
var raw: List[List[i64]] = []
var cur: List[i64] = []
for c in n
if c == 46
raw.push(cur)
cur = []
else
cur.push(c)
raw.push(cur)
var err = false
var out: List[List[i64]] = []
for l in raw
if is_xn(&l)
if not all_ascii(&l)
err = true
out.push(copy(l))
continue
var rest: List[i64] = []
var k: usize = 4
while k < l.len() bound 16777216
rest.push(l[k])
k += 1
let d = puny_decode(&rest)
if d.err
if not f.ignore_bad_punycode
err = true
out.push(copy(l))
continue
if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
err = true
out.push(copy(l))
continue
if d.cps.len() == 0 or all_ascii(&d.cps)
err = true
if not valid_label(&d.cps, f, false, true)
err = true
out.push(d.cps)
else
if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
err = true
out.push(copy(l))
if f.bidi
var rtl = false
for l in out
if is_rtl_label(&l)
rtl = true
if rtl
for l in out
if not bidi_ok(&l)
err = true
return Labels(labels: out, err: err)

fn join_dots(ls: &[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 0
while i < ls.len() bound 16777216
if i > 0
o.push(46)
for c in ls[i]
o.push(c)
i += 1
return o

module net.idna

# UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing (revision 33, Unicode
# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,
# normalize to NFC (UAX #15, canonical decomposition, reordering and
# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
std3: bool
hyphens: bool
bidi: bool
joiners: bool
transitional: bool
dns_length: bool
ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps
cps: List[i64]
err: bool

pub struct Ascii
host: text
err: bool

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)
if c >= S_BASE and c < S_BASE + S_COUNT
let s = c - S_BASE
o.push(L_BASE + s / N_COUNT)
o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)
if s % T_COUNT != 0
o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)
return
let d = decomposition(c)
if d.len() == 0
o.push(c)
return
for x in d
o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
for c in cps
decompose_into(&mut o, c)
var cc: List[i64] = []
for c in o
cc.push(ccc(c))
# stable insertion sort of each run of non-starters by class
var i: usize = 1
while i < o.len() bound 16777216
var j = i
while j > 0 and cc[j] != 0 and cc[j - 1] > cc[j] bound 16777216
let t = o[j]
o[j] = o[j - 1]
o[j - 1] = t
let u = cc[j]
cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
cc[j - 1] = u
j -= 1
i += 1
return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
if a >= L_BASE and a < L_BASE + 19 and b >= V_BASE and b < V_BASE + 21
return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT
if a >= S_BASE and a < S_BASE + S_COUNT and (a - S_BASE) % T_COUNT == 0 and b > T_BASE and b < T_BASE + T_COUNT
return a + (b - T_BASE)
return composite(a * 1114112 + b)

pub fn nfc(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
let d = nfd(cps)
var o: List[i64] = []
if d.len() == 0
return o
var sp: usize = 0
var last = ccc(d[0])
var starter = last == 0

while i < d.len() bound 16777216
let c = d[i]
let cl = ccc(c)
let comp = if starter then compose_pair(o[sp], c) else -1
if starter and (last < cl or last == 0) and comp >= 0
o[sp] = comp
i += 1
continue
if cl == 0
sp = o.len()
starter = true
last = cl
o.push(c)
i += 1
return o

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1
const P_TMAX: i64 = 26
const P_MAX: i64 = 2147483647

fn adapt(delta0: i64, numpoints: i64, first: bool) -> i64
var delta = if first then delta0 / 700 else delta0 / 2
delta += delta / numpoints

while delta > ((P_BASE - P_TMIN) * P_TMAX) / 2 bound 64
delta = delta / (P_BASE - P_TMIN)
k += P_BASE
return k + (P_BASE - P_TMIN + 1) * delta / (delta + 38)

fn digit_value(c: i64) -> i64
if c >= 48 and c <= 57
return c - 22
if c >= 65 and c <= 90
return c - 65
if c >= 97 and c <= 122
return c - 97
return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
if k <= bias
return P_TMIN
if k >= bias + P_TMAX
return P_TMAX
return k - bias

# Decoding; a failure (bad digit, end inside a number, overflow, a
# result that is not a scalar value) gives err.
pub fn puny_decode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps

while j < input.len() bound 16777216
if input[j] == 45
b = j
j += 1

while k < b bound 16777216
if input[k] >= 128
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
o.push(input[k])
k += 1
var p: usize = if b > 0 then b + 1 else 0
var n: i64 = 128
var i: i64 = 0
var bias: i64 = 72
while p < input.len() bound 16777216
let oldi = i
var w: i64 = 1
var kk: i64 = P_BASE
loop bound 64
if p >= input.len()

p += 1

bias = adapt(i - oldi, len, oldi == 0)
if i / len > P_MAX - n
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
n += i / len
i = i % len
if n > 1114111 or (n >= 55296 and n <= 57343)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
o.push(n)

while q > i as usize bound 16777216
o[q] = o[q - 1]
q -= 1

i += 1
return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
var o: List[i64] = []
for c in input
if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
if c < 128
o.push(c)
let basic = o.len() as i64
var h = basic
if basic > 0
o.push(45)
var n: i64 = 128
var delta: i64 = 0
var bias: i64 = 72
let total = input.len() as i64

var m: i64 = P_MAX
for c in input
if c >= n and c < m
m = c
if m - n > (P_MAX - delta) / (h + 1)
return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
delta += (m - n) * (h + 1)
n = m
for c in input
if c < n
delta += 1
if delta > P_MAX

# ---------------- UTS #46 processing ----------------

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool
for c in l
if c >= 128
return false
return true

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
for c in l
let b = bidi_class(c)
if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
return true
return false

# RFC 5893 section 2, rules 1 to 6, for one label of a bidi domain.
pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool

return true
let f = bidi_class(l[0])
if f != 0 and f != 1 and f != 2
return false

var an = false

let b = bidi_class(c)

return false
if b == 4
en = true
if b == 3
an = true
if en and an
return false
return last == 1 or last == 2 or last == 4 or last == 3

# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 (ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER) and A.2 (ZERO WIDTH JOINER).
pub fn joiners_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool

let c = l[i]
if c == 8204 or c == 8205
let virama = i > 0 and ccc(l[i - 1]) == 9
if not virama
if c == 8205
return false
var a = i
var left = false
while a > 0 bound 16777216
let t = joining_type(l[a - 1])
if t == 5
a -= 1
continue
left = t == 2 or t == 4
break
var z = i + 1
var right = false
while z < l.len() bound 16777216
let t = joining_type(l[z])
if t == 5
z += 1
continue
right = t == 2 or t == 3
break
if not (left and right)
return false
i += 1
return true

# Validity criteria 4.1 except the bidi rules (checked per domain).
fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool
if l.len() == 0
return true
if decoded

if n != copy(l)
return false
if f.hyphens
if l.len() >= 4 and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

return false

if not (s == 0 or (s == 2 and not transitional))

return false
if f.joiners and not joiners_ok(l)
return false
return true

pub struct Labels

err: bool

fn join_dots(ls: &[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
var o: List[i64] = []
var i: usize = 0
while i < ls.len() bound 16777216
if i > 0

# 4.3 ToUnicode.
pub fn to_unicode(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
let p = process(input, f)

module num.linalg

# Dense real linear algebra over IEEE 754 binary64 (survey workstream A).
#
# Determinism. Every result is a fixed sequence of correctly rounded
# + - * / and sqrt (spec 6.3 N3: one result per operation on every
# target, no FMA contraction), so a call gives the same bits on every
# emit target. The order of every reduction is fixed and documented, and
# it is the order of the Reference BLAS and LAPACK 3.12.1 routine each
# function ports: a sum runs left to right in increasing index unless the
# routine says otherwise. Ported routines are checked bit for bit against
# Reference LAPACK 3.12.1 (tests/num/linalg_checks*.rce).
#
# Storage. A matrix is column major, element (i, j) of an m x n matrix at
# a[i + j * m] (0-based), like LAPACK with lda = m. Functions on raw
# storage take an offset and a leading dimension (or stride) so the
# LAPACK index arithmetic carries over unchanged.
#
# Non-finite values trap like every f64 operation (6.3 N3), so NaN and
# infinity never appear; the NaN branches of LAPACK are dead here.

pub struct Mat
m: usize
n: usize
a: List[f64]

# One error type: why is "shape", "singular" (at = 0-based column of the
# first zero pivot) or "not positive definite" (at = failing column).
error LaError(why: text, at: i64)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- model
# Binary64 parameters (LAPACK DLAMCH): eps = 2^-53 ('E', round to
# nearest), safe minimum = 2^-1022 ('S'), overflow = (1 - 2^-53) 2^1024.

pub fn la_pow2(k: i64) -> f64
var r = 1.0
var i: i64 = 0
if k >= 0
while i < k bound 1100
r = r * 2.0
i += 1
else
while i > k bound 1100
r = r * 0.5
i -= 1
return r

pub const LA_EPS: f64 = 1.1102230246251565e-16
pub const LA_SFMIN: f64 = 2.2250738585072014e-308
pub const LA_HUGE: f64 = 1.7976931348623157e308

pub fn la_abs(x: f64) -> f64 = if x < 0.0 then 0.0 - x else x

# Fortran SIGN(a, b): |a| with the sign of b (b >= 0 counts as positive;
# there is no negative zero).
pub fn la_sign(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 = if b >= 0.0 then la_abs(a) else 0.0 - la_abs(a)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- BLAS 1
# Vectors are (list, offset, stride); strides are positive.

# DDOT: sum of x[i] * y[i], i = 0..n-1 in order (the unrolled reference
# loop associates left to right, so it is the same order).
pub fn ddot(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, y: &[f64], oy: usize, iy: usize) -> f64
var t = 0.0
for i in 0..n
t = t + x[ox + i * ix] * y[oy + i * iy]
return t

# DAXPY: y := y + alpha * x (no-op when alpha == 0).
pub fn daxpy(n: usize, alpha: f64, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, y: &mut List[f64], oy: usize, iy: usize)
if alpha == 0.0
return
for i in 0..n
y[oy + i * iy] = y[oy + i * iy] + alpha * x[ox + i * ix]

# DSCAL: x := alpha * x.
pub fn dscal(n: usize, alpha: f64, x: &mut List[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize)
for i in 0..n
x[ox + i * ix] = alpha * x[ox + i * ix]

# DSWAP.
pub fn dswap(n: usize, x: &mut List[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, oy: usize, iy: usize)
for i in 0..n
let t = x[ox + i * ix]
x[ox + i * ix] = x[oy + i * iy]
x[oy + i * iy] = t

# DASUM: sum of |x[i]| in order.
pub fn dasum(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> f64
var t = 0.0
for i in 0..n
t = t + la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])
return t

# IDAMAX: first index (0-based) of the largest |x[i]|; 0 for n == 0.
pub fn idamax(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> usize
var k: usize = 0
if n == 0
return 0
var mx = la_abs(x[ox])
for i in 1..n
let v = la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])
if v > mx
k = i
mx = v
return k

# DNRM2 of Reference BLAS 3.10+ (Anderson 2017, Blue's three
# accumulators): no overflow or harmful underflow for any finite input.
# tsml = 2^-511, tbig = 2^486, ssml = 2^537, sbig = 2^-538.
pub fn dnrm2(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> f64
if n == 0
return 0.0
let tsml = la_pow2(-511)
let tbig = la_pow2(486)
let ssml = la_pow2(537)
let sbig = la_pow2(-538)

var asml = 0.0
var amed = 0.0

for i in 0..n
let ax = la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])

elif ax < tsml
if notbig

amed = amed + ax * ax

if amed > 0.0
abig = abig + (amed * sbig) * sbig

sumsq = abig
