pub fn orm2r_b(w: &mut List[f64], trans: bool, m: usize, n: usize, k: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize, otau: usize, oc: usize, ldc: usize, owork: usize)
for s in 0..k
let i = if trans then s else k - 1 - s
larf1f_b(w, true, m - i, n, oa + i + i * lda, 1, w[otau + i], oc + i, ldc, owork)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- matrices

pub fn mat(m: usize, n: usize, a: List[f64]) -> Mat ! LaError
if a.len() != m * n
fail LaError(why: "data length is not m * n", at: -1)
return Mat(m: m, n: n, a: a)

# From row-major data (the order matrices are usually written in).
pub fn from_rows(m: usize, n: usize, r: &[f64]) -> Mat ! LaError
if r.len() != m * n
fail LaError(why: "data length is not m * n", at: -1)
var a: List[f64] = []
for j in 0..n
for i in 0..m
a.push(r[i * n + j])
return Mat(m: m, n: n, a: a)

pub fn to_rows(x: &Mat) -> List[f64]
var r: List[f64] = []
for i in 0..x.m
for j in 0..x.n
r.push(x.a[i + j * x.m])
return r

pub fn zeros(m: usize, n: usize) -> Mat
var a: List[f64] = []
for _ in 0..(m * n)
a.push(0.0)
return Mat(m: m, n: n, a: a)

pub fn eye(n: usize) -> Mat
var z = zeros(n, n)
for i in 0..n
z.a[i + i * n] = 1.0
return z

pub fn mat_at(x: &Mat, i: usize, j: usize) -> f64 = x.a[i + j * x.m]

pub fn transpose(x: &Mat) -> Mat
var a: List[f64] = []
for i in 0..x.m
for j in 0..x.n
a.push(x.a[i + j * x.m])
return Mat(m: x.n, n: x.m, a: a)

pub fn mat_col(x: &Mat, j: usize) -> List[f64]
var c: List[f64] = []
for i in 0..x.m
c.push(x.a[i + j * x.m])
return c

fn la_cat(a: &[f64], b: &[f64]) -> List[f64]
var w: List[f64] = []
for v in a
w.push(v)
for v in b
w.push(v)
return w

fn la_slice(w: &[f64], o: usize, n: usize) -> List[f64]
var r: List[f64] = []
for i in 0..n
r.push(w[o + i])
return r

# C = alpha op(A) op(B) + beta C (DGEMM order).
pub fn gemm(ta: bool, tb: bool, alpha: f64, a: &Mat, b: &Mat, beta: f64, c: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
let m = if ta then a.n else a.m
let k = if ta then a.m else a.n
let kb = if tb then b.n else b.m
let n = if tb then b.m else b.n
if k != kb or c.m != m or c.n != n
fail LaError(why: "gemm dimensions", at: -1)
let ob = a.a.len()
let oc = ob + b.a.len()
let ab = la_cat(&a.a, &b.a)
var w = la_cat(&ab, &c.a)
gemm_b(&mut w, ta, tb, m, n, k, alpha, 0, a.m, ob, b.m, beta, oc, m)
return Mat(m: m, n: n, a: la_slice(&w, oc, m * n))

pub fn matmul(a: &Mat, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
let c = zeros(a.m, b.n)
return try gemm(false, false, 1.0, a, b, 0.0, &c)

# y = alpha op(A) x + beta y (DGEMV order).
pub fn gemv(trans: bool, alpha: f64, a: &Mat, x: &[f64], beta: f64, y: &[f64]) -> List[f64] ! LaError
let lx = if trans then a.m else a.n
let ly = if trans then a.n else a.m
if x.len() != lx or y.len() != ly
fail LaError(why: "gemv dimensions", at: -1)
let ox = a.a.len()
let oy = ox + x.len()
let ax = la_cat(&a.a, x)
var w = la_cat(&ax, y)
gemv_b(&mut w, trans, a.m, a.n, alpha, 0, a.m, ox, 1, beta, oy, 1)
return la_slice(&w, oy, ly)

pub fn matvec(a: &Mat, x: &[f64]) -> List[f64] ! LaError
var y: List[f64] = []
for _ in 0..a.m
y.push(0.0)
return try gemv(false, 1.0, a, x, 0.0, &y)

# A + alpha x y^T (DGER order).
pub fn ger(alpha: f64, x: &[f64], y: &[f64], a: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
if x.len() != a.m or y.len() != a.n
fail LaError(why: "ger dimensions", at: -1)
let ox = a.a.len()
let oy = ox + x.len()
let ax = la_cat(&a.a, x)
var w = la_cat(&ax, y)
ger_b(&mut w, a.m, a.n, alpha, ox, 1, oy, 1, 0, a.m)
return Mat(m: a.m, n: a.n, a: la_slice(&w, 0, a.a.len()))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- LU

pub struct Lu
lu: Mat
piv: List[i64]
info: i64

# P A = L U (DGETF2). info > 0 marks an exact zero pivot (U singular).
pub fn lu(a: &Mat) -> Lu
var w = copy(a.a)
var piv: List[i64] = []
let info = getf2_b(&mut w, a.m, a.n, 0, a.m, &mut piv)
return Lu(lu: Mat(m: a.m, n: a.n, a: w), piv: piv, info: info)

# Solve A X = B (trans false) or A^T X = B from a square LU (DGETRS).
pub fn lu_solve(f: &Lu, trans: bool, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
let n = f.lu.n
if f.lu.m != n or b.m != n
fail LaError(why: "lu_solve dimensions", at: -1)
if f.info > 0
fail LaError(why: "singular", at: f.info - 1)
let ob = n * n
var w = la_cat(&f.lu.a, &b.a)
if not trans
laswp_b(&mut w, b.n, ob, n, 0, n, &f.piv, true)
trsm_b(&mut w, false, false, true, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
trsm_b(&mut w, true, false, false, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
else
trsm_b(&mut w, true, true, false, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
trsm_b(&mut w, false, true, true, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
laswp_b(&mut w, b.n, ob, n, 0, n, &f.piv, false)
return Mat(m: n, n: b.n, a: la_slice(&w, ob, n * b.n))

pub fn solve(a: &Mat, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
if a.m != a.n
fail LaError(why: "solve needs a square matrix", at: -1)
let f = lu(a)
return try lu_solve(&f, false, b)

# Inverse as the solution of A X = I (DGETRS on the identity).
pub fn inv(a: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
let i = eye(a.n)
return try solve(a, &i)

# Determinant: product of the U diagonal in increasing index, negated
# once per row swap.
pub fn det(a: &Mat) -> f64 ! LaError
if a.m != a.n
fail LaError(why: "det needs a square matrix", at: -1)
let f = lu(a)
var d = 1.0
for i in 0..a.n
d = d * f.lu.a[i + i * a.n]
if f.piv[i] != i as i64
d = 0.0 - d
return d

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Cholesky

# A = L L^T for symmetric positive definite A (DPOTF2, lower; only the
# lower triangle of A is read). L is returned with a zero upper triangle.
pub fn chol(a: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
if a.m != a.n
fail LaError(why: "chol needs a square matrix", at: -1)
let n = a.n
var w = copy(a.a)
let info = potf2_b(&mut w, n, 0, n)
if info > 0
fail LaError(why: "not positive definite", at: info - 1)
for j in 0..n
for i in 0..j
w[i + j * n] = 0.0
return Mat(m: n, n: n, a: w)

# Solve A X = B from L (DPOTRS, lower).
pub fn chol_solve(l: &Mat, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
let n = l.n
if l.m != n or b.m != n
fail LaError(why: "chol_solve dimensions", at: -1)
let ob = n * n
var w = la_cat(&l.a, &b.a)
trsm_b(&mut w, false, false, false, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
trsm_b(&mut w, false, true, false, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
return Mat(m: n, n: b.n, a: la_slice(&w, ob, n * b.n))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- QR

pub struct Qr
qr: Mat
tau: List[f64]

# A = Q R, Householder (DGEQR2): R in the upper triangle of qr, the
# reflectors below it.
pub fn qr(a: &Mat) -> Qr
let m = a.m
let n = a.n
let k = if m < n then m else n
let ot = m * n
let ow = ot + k
var w = copy(a.a)
for _ in 0..(k + n)
w.push(0.0)
geqr2_b(&mut w, m, n, 0, m, ot, ow)
return Qr(qr: Mat(m: m, n: n, a: la_slice(&w, 0, m * n)), tau: la_slice(&w, ot, k))

# The m x k orthonormal factor (DORG2R), k = min(m, n).
pub fn qr_q(f: &Qr) -> Mat
let m = f.qr.m
let k = f.tau.len()
let ot = m * k
var w = la_slice(&f.qr.a, 0, m * k)
for t in &f.tau
w.push(t)
for _ in 0..k
w.push(0.0)
org2r_b(&mut w, m, k, k, 0, m, ot, ot + k)
return Mat(m: m, n: k, a: la_slice(&w, 0, m * k))

# The k x n upper triangular factor.
pub fn qr_r(f: &Qr) -> Mat
let m = f.qr.m
let n = f.qr.n
let k = f.tau.len()
var r = zeros(k, n)
for j in 0..n
for i in 0..k
if i <= j
r.a[i + j * k] = f.qr.a[i + j * m]
return r

# Least squares min ||A X - B|| for m >= n and full rank (DGELS 'N' for
# matrices below the blocking crossover: DGEQR2, DORM2R, DTRTRS; the
# DGELS rescaling only acts outside [SFMIN/EPS, EPS/SFMIN] and is not
# reproduced: such inputs are refused with Shape).
pub fn lstsq(a: &Mat, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
let m = a.m
let n = a.n
if m < n or b.m != m
fail LaError(why: "lstsq needs m >= n and b with m rows", at: -1)
var amax = 0.0
for v in &a.a
amax = amax.max(la_abs(v))
let smlnum = LA_SFMIN / (2.0 * LA_EPS)
if amax == 0.0 or amax < smlnum or amax > 1.0 / smlnum
fail LaError(why: "lstsq: A is zero or outside the unscaled range", at: -1)
let nrhs = b.n
let ot = m * n
let ob = ot + n
let ow = ob + m * nrhs
let z = zeros(n, 1)
let az = la_cat(&a.a, &z.a)
var w = la_cat(&az, &b.a)
let wl = if n > nrhs then n else nrhs
for _ in 0..wl
w.push(0.0)
geqr2_b(&mut w, m, n, 0, m, ot, ow)
orm2r_b(&mut w, true, m, nrhs, n, 0, m, ot, ob, m, ow)
for i in 0..n
if w[i + i * m] == 0.0
fail LaError(why: "singular", at: i as i64)
trsm_b(&mut w, true, false, false, n, nrhs, 1.0, 0, m, ob, m)
var x = zeros(n, nrhs)
for j in 0..nrhs
for i in 0..n
x.a[i + j * n] = w[ob + i + j * m]
return x

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Jacobi
# Symmetric eigenproblem and SVD by Jacobi rotations (Jacobi 1846;
# Rutishauser's update, Handbook for Automatic Computation II/1; one-sided
# form of Hestenes 1958). Chosen over QR iteration because Jacobi computes
# small eigenvalues and singular values of well-scaled matrices to high
# relative accuracy (Demmel and Veselic, SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 13,
# 1992) and its sweep order is a fixed, simple sequence. Order: cyclic by
# rows, (p, q) = (0, 1), (0, 2), .., (0, n-1), (1, 2), ..; a sweep without
# a rotation ends the iteration (at most 80 sweeps). Rotation for a pivot
# with off-diagonal g and diagonal (or squared column norms) a, b:
# zeta = (b - a) / (2 g), t = sign(zeta) / (|zeta| + sqrt(1 + zeta^2)),
# c = 1 / sqrt(1 + t^2), s = c t (|zeta| > 2^500: t = 1 / (2 zeta)).
# A pivot is skipped when |g| <= EPS sqrt(|a| |b|) (the relative
# criterion), and also when |g| is below SFMIN / EPS.

fn la_rot(a: f64, b: f64, g: f64) -> List[f64]
let zeta = (b - a) / (2.0 * g)
var t = 0.0
if la_abs(zeta) > la_pow2(500)
t = 1.0 / (2.0 * zeta)
else
t = la_sign(1.0, zeta) / (la_abs(zeta) + (1.0 + zeta * zeta).sqrt())
let c = 1.0 / (1.0 + t * t).sqrt()
return [c, c * t, t]

pub struct Eigh
values: List[f64]
vectors: Mat

# Sort key order: ascending (asc) or descending; ties keep index order.
fn la_order(v: &[f64], asc: bool) -> List[usize]
var idx: List[usize] = []
for i in 0..v.len()
idx.push(i)
for i in 0..v.len()
var best = i
for j in (i + 1)..v.len()
let better = if asc then v[idx[j]] < v[idx[best]] else v[idx[j]] > v[idx[best]]
if better
best = j
let t = idx[i]
idx[i] = idx[best]
idx[best] = t
return idx

# Sign convention for a computed vector: the entry of largest magnitude
# (first one on ties) is made positive.
fn la_fix_sign(w: &mut List[f64], o: usize, n: usize)
let k k = idamax(n, w, o, 1)
if w[o + k] < 0.0
for i in 0..n
w[o + i] = 0.0 - w[o + i]

# Eigenvalues (ascending) and orthonormal eigenvectors (columns) of a
# symmetric matrix; only the lower triangle is read.
pub fn eigh(a: &Mat) -> Eigh ! LaError
if a.m != a.n
fail LaError(why: "eigh needs a square matrix", at: -1)
let n = a.n
var w: List[f64] = []
for j in 0..n
for i in 0..n
w.push(if i >= j then a.a[i + j * n] else a.a[j + i * n])
var v = eye(n).a
var sweep = 0
while sweep < 80 bound 81
sweep += 1
var rotated = false
for p in 0..n
for q in (p + 1)..n
let g = w[p + q * n]
let app = w[p + p * n]
let aqq = w[q + q * n]
if la_abs(g) > LA_EPS * (la_abs(app) * la_abs(aqq)).sqrt() and la_abs(g) > LA_SFMIN / LA_EPS
rotated = true
let r = la_rot(app, aqq, g)
let c = r[0]
let s = r[1]
let t = r[2]
w[p + p * n] = app - t * g
w[q + q * n] = aqq + t * g
w[p + q * n] = 0.0
w[q + p * n] = 0.0
for k in 0..n
if k != p and k != q
let akp = w[k + p * n]
let akq = w[k + q * n]
let np = c * akp - s * akq
let nq = s * akp + c * akq
w[k + p * n] = np
w[p + k * n] = np
w[k + q * n] = nq
w[q + k * n] = nq
for k in 0..n
let vkp = v[k + p * n]
let vkq = v[k + q * n]
v[k + p * n] = c * vkp - s * vkq
v[k + q * n] = s * vkp + c * vkq
if not rotated
break
var d: List[f64] = []
for i in 0..n
d.push(w[i + i * n])
let idx = la_order(&d, true)
var vals: List[f64] = []
var vs: List[f64] = []
for j in 0..n
vals.push(d[idx[j]])
for i in 0..n
vs.push(v[i + idx[j] * n])
la_fix_sign(&mut vs, j * n, n)
return Eigh(values: vals, vectors: Mat(m: n, n: n, a: vs))

# One-sided rotation from the column norms np, nq and their cosine cs:
# zeta = (nq/np - np/nq) / (2 cs); when the norms differ by more than
# 2^500, t = cs nq/np or -cs np/nq (the first-order value, exact to
# working precision there).
fn la_rot2(np: f64, nq: f64, cs: f64) -> List[f64]
var t = 0.0
let big = la_pow2(500)
if np < nq and nq / big > np
t = cs * (np / nq)
elif nq < np and np / big > nq
t = 0.0 - cs * (nq / np)
else
let zeta = (nq / np - np / nq) / (2.0 * cs)
if la_abs(zeta) > big
t = 1.0 / (2.0 * zeta)
else
t = la_sign(1.0, zeta) / (la_abs(zeta) + (1.0 + zeta * zeta).sqrt())
let c = 1.0 / (1.0 + t * t).sqrt()
return [c, c * t]

# Complete the columns j with zero singular value to an orthonormal set:
# column j becomes the standard basis vector e_i (smallest i among those
# with the largest residual) orthogonalized twice (classical Gram-Schmidt,
# DDOT order) against the columns already set, then normalized.
fn la_complete(u: &mut List[f64], m: usize, k: usize, s: &[f64])
var done: List[usize] = []
for j in 0..k
if s[j] > 0.0
done.push(j)
for j in 0..k
if s[j] > 0.0
continue
var best: List[f64] = []
var bn = -1.0
for i in 0..m
var x: List[f64] = []
for r in 0..m
x.push(if r == i then 1.0 else 0.0)
for _ in 0..2
for c in &done
let d = ddot(m, u, c * m, 1, &x, 0, 1)
for r in 0..m
x[r] = x[r] - d * u[r + c * m]
let xn = dnrm2(m, &x, 0, 1)
if xn > bn
bn = xn
best = x
for r in 0..m
u[r + j * m] = best[r] / bn
done.push(j)

pub struct Svd
u: Mat
s: List[f64]
v: Mat

# Thin SVD A = U diag(s) V^T, s descending, k = min(m, n): U m x k, V n x
# k. One-sided Jacobi on the columns (on A^T when m < n). The matrix is
# first scaled by a power of two (exact) so its largest entry is in
# [1, 2). At every pivot the column norms are recomputed (DNRM2) and the
# cosine is the DDOT-order sum of the normalized entries, so neither
# underflows for badly scaled columns; the pivot is skipped when
# |cos| <= EPS. A U column whose (scaled) singular value is below
# SFMIN / EPS has no reliable direction (its entries are subnormal); it
# and the columns of zero singular values are completed to an
# orthonormal basis (la_complete).
pub fn svd(a: &Mat) -> Svd
if a.m < a.n
let tr = transpose(a)
let r = la_svd_tall(&tr)
return Svd(u: copy(r.v), s: copy(r.s), v: copy(r.u))
return la_svd_tall(a)

fn la_svd_tall(a: &Mat) -> Svd
let m = a.m
let n = a.n
var amax = 0.0
for x in &a.a
amax = amax.max(la_abs(x))
var e: i64 = 0
var sc = 1.0
if amax > 0.0
while amax * sc >= 2.0 bound 1100
sc = sc * 0.5
e += 1
while amax * sc < 1.0 bound 1100
sc = sc * 2.0
e -= 1
var w: List[f64] = []
for x in &a.a
w.push(x * sc)
var v = eye(n).a
var sweep = 0
while sweep < 80 bound 81
sweep += 1
var rotated = false
for p in 0..n
for q in (p + 1)..n
let np = dnrm2(m, &w, p * m, 1)
let nq = dnrm2(m, &w, q * m, 1)
var cs = 0.0
if np > 0.0 and nq > 0.0
for k in 0..m
cs = cs + (w[k + p * m] / np) * (w[k + q * m] / nq)
if la_abs(cs) > LA_EPS
rotated = true
let r = la_rot2(np, nq, cs)
let c = r[0]
let s = r[1]
for k in 0..m
let x = w[k + p * m]
let y = w[k + q * m]
w[k + p * m] = c * x - s * y
w[k + q * m] = s * x + c * y
for k in 0..n
let x = v[k + p * n]
let y = v[k + q * n]
v[k + p * n] = c * x - s * y
v[k + q * n] = s * x + c * y
if not rotated
break
var sv: List[f64] = []
for j in 0..n
sv.push(dnrm2(m, &w, j * m, 1))
let idx = la_order(&sv, false)
let unsc = la_pow2(e)
let tiny = LA_SFMIN / LA_EPS
var s: List[f64] = []
var live: List[f64] = []
var u: List[f64] = []
var vv: List[f64] = []
for j in 0..n
let k = idx[j]
let sj = sv[k]
s.push(sj * unsc)
live.push(if sj >= tiny then sj else 0.0)
for i in 0..m
u.push(if sj >= tiny then w[i + k * m] / sj else 0.0)
for i in 0..n
vv.push(v[i + k * n])
let ku = idamax(m, &u, j * m, 1)
let kv = idamax(n, &vv, j * n, 1)
let neg = if sj >= tiny then u[j * m + ku] < 0.0 else vv[j * n + kv] < 0.0
if neg
for i in 0..m
u[j * m + i] = 0.0 - u[j * m + i]
for i in 0..n
vv[j * n + i] = 0.0 - vv[j * n + i]
la_complete(&mut u, m, n, &live)
return Svd(u: Mat(m: m, n: n, a: u), s: s, v: Mat(m: n, n: n, a: vv))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- nonsymmetric eigenvalues
# Eigenvalues of a general real matrix as Reference LAPACK 3.12.1 DGEEV
# computes them without vectors for n below its blocking crossovers
# (n <= 32 here): DGEBAL ('B': permute, then scale by powers of 2),
# DGEHD2 (Householder Hessenberg reduction), DHSEQR -> DLAHQR (double
# shift QR, exceptional shifts every 10 iterations, the Ahues and Tisseur
# deflation test) with DLANV2 for 2 x 2 blocks. Indices below are 1-based
# as in the Fortran so the port reads line for line.

fn fx(i: i64, j: i64, ld: i64) -> usize = ((i - 1) + (j - 1) * ld) as usize

pub struct Balanced
ilo: i64
ihi: i64
scale: List[f64]

# DGEBAL, job 'B', in place on the n x n matrix at w[0..].
pub fn gebal_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: i64) -> Balanced
var scale: List[f64] = []
for _ in 0..n
scale.push(1.0)
if n == 0
return Balanced(ilo: 1, ihi: 0, scale: scale)
var k: i64 = 1
var l: i64 = n
var noconv = true
while noconv bound 1048576
noconv = false
let l0 = l
var i = l0
while i >= 1 bound 1048576
var canswap = true
var j: i64 = 1
while j <= l bound 1048576
if i != j and w[fx(i, j, n)] != 0.0
canswap = false
break
j += 1
if canswap
scale[(l - 1) as usize] = i as f64

module os.clock

# Clocks and timers (survey M37), pure. A program never reads a clock: the
# host admits each monotonic or wall reading as a logged event, and it
# admits each timer firing as an event in D order, so replay is exact.
# This module holds what a program does with those values:
# - Dur, Rust's core::time::Duration (secs plus nanos below one second)
# with its constructors, accessors, checked and saturating arithmetic and
# its Debug formatting ("1.5s", "7.1µs", precision, width, alignment).
# Secs are u64 as in Rust, so the full range holds.
# - Timespec, the point type behind Rust's unix Instant and SystemTime
# (secs i64, nanos 0..1e9), with checked and saturating add/sub and
# duration_since in Rust's forms (saturating, checked, signed result).
# - wasi:clocks@0.2.8 values: a monotonic instant (u64 ns) and a wall
# datetime (seconds, nanoseconds < 1e9) mapped to Timespec.
# - Mono, the admission rule for monotonic readings: a reading below the
# last admitted one is raised to it (non-decreasing, as wasi-clocks
# promises and as Rust's monotonize enforces).
# - Timers, the pure timer queue: subscribe at an instant or after a
# duration; a tick at `now` fires every due timer in (deadline, subscribe
# order) order. The host admits those firings as events in that order.

error BadClock(why: text)

pub const NPS: u64 = 1000000000
pub const MAX_U: u64 = 18446744073709551615
pub const MAX_SECS: i64 = 9223372036854775807
pub const MIN_SECS: i64 = -9223372036854775808

pub struct Dur

pub fn dur_max() -> Dur = Dur(secs: MAX_U, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

pub fn from_millis(ms: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ms / 1000, nanos: (ms % 1000) as i64 * 1000000)
pub fn from_micros(us: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: us / 1000000, nanos: (us % 1000000) as i64 * 1000)

next: i64

pub fn timers_new() -> Timers = Timers(list: [], next: 0)

fn before(a: &Timer, b: &Timer) -> bool
let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
q.next += 1

var placed = false
for x in q.list
if not placed and before(&t, &x)

placed = true
out.push(copy(x))
if not placed
out.push(copy(t))
q.list = out

pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
var out: List[Timer] = []
var hit = false
for x in q.list
if x.id == id
hit = true
else
out.push(copy(x))
q.list = out
return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
if q.list.len() == 0
return none
return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
var ids: List[i64] = []
var rest: List[Timer] = []
for x in q.list
if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
ids.push(x.id)
else
rest.push(copy(x))
q.list = rest
return ids

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
# - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
# preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
# position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
# with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
# renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
# preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
# not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
# holes and timestamps are not modelled.
# - the error-code  of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
# names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.
pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
var i: i64 = 0
for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
if x == c
return i
i += 1
return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
let i = code_index(c)
if i < 0
return ""
return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

pub fn code_of_errno(e: text) -> text
var i: usize = 0
let es = ERRNOS.split(" ")
while i < es.len() bound 64
if es[i] == e
return copy(ERROR_CODES.split(" ")[i])
i += 1
return ""

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
dir: bool
data: List[text]
parent: i64

pub struct Ent
dir: i64
name: text
nd: i64

pub struct Desc
nd: i64
pos: i64
rd: bool
wr: bool
app: bool
live: bool

pub struct Fs
nodes: List[Node]
ents: List[Ent]
descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
for e in fs.ents
if e.dir == d and e.name == name
return e.nd
return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
for e in fs.ents
if e.dir == d
return false
return true

# Where a path leads: the directory holding the last component, the last
# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
dir: i64
last: text
nd: i64
slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
var o: List[text] = []
for c in path.split("/")
if c != ""
o.push(c)
return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
fail bad("not-directory")
if c == "."
return cur
if c == ".."
let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
if p < 0
fail bad("not-permitted")
return p
let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
if n < 0
fail bad("no-entry")
return n

# follow: whether a final "." or ".." is stepped (open, stat, list); the
# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
if path == ""
fail bad("no-entry")
if path.startswith("/")
fail bad("not-permitted")
let cs = comps(path)
var cur: i64 = 0
var i: usize = 0
while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
i += 1
if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
fail bad("not-directory")
let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
var nd: i64 = -1
if last == "." or last == ".."
if follow
nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
else
nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn named(w: &Where) -> bool = w.last != "." and w.last != ".."

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64
fs.nodes.push(Node(dir: dir, data: [], parent: parent))
return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
var o: List[Ent] = []
for e in fs.ents
if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
o.push(copy(e))
fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
fail bad("exist")
let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
return true

# Open flags as text: r (read), w (write), c (create), x (exclusive),
# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
let rd = flags.contains("r")
let wr = flags.contains("w")
let cr = flags.contains("c")
let ex = flags.contains("x")
let tr = flags.contains("t")
let dr = flags.contains("d")
if cr and dr
fail bad("invalid")
let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
fail bad("is-directory")
var n = w.nd
if n < 0
if not cr

n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)

elif cr and ex
fail bad("exist")
elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
if wr or cr or tr
fail bad("is-directory")

if dr or w.slash
fail bad("not-directory")

fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
fail bad("bad-descriptor")
return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

pub fn read(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, n: i64) -> text ! FsErr
let d = try desc(fs, h)
if not d.rd
fail bad("bad-descriptor")
if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
fail bad("is-directory")
let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
var o = ""
var p = d.pos
while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
o = o + data[p as usize]
p += 1
fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
let d = try desc(fs, h)
if not d.wr
fail bad("bad-descriptor")
var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
var p = if d.app then data.len() as i64 else d.pos
while data.len() as i64 < p bound 16777216
data.push("\u{0}")
for c in s.chars()
if p < data.len() as i64
data[p as usize] = c
else
data.push(c)
p += 1
fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = data
fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
return true

pub fn seek(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, pos: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
let _d = try desc(fs, h)
if pos < 0
fail bad("invalid")
fs.descs[h as usize].pos = pos
return true

pub fn truncate(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, len: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
let d = try desc(fs, h)
if not d.wr or len < 0
fail bad("invalid")
var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
var o: List[text] = []
var i: i64 = 0

o.push(if i < data.len() as i64 then copy(data[i as usize]) else "\u{0}")

fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = o
return true

pub fn close(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
let _d = try desc(fs, h)
fs.descs[h as usize].live = false
return true

pub fn unlink_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
if not named(&w)
fail bad("is-directory")
if w.nd < 0
fail bad("no-entry")
if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
fail bad("is-directory")
if w.slash
fail bad("not-directory")
drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
return true

pub fn rmdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
if w.last == "."
fail bad("invalid")
if w.last == ".."
fail bad("not-empty")
if w.nd < 0
fail bad("no-entry")
if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir

if not is_empty(fs, w.nd)
fail bad("not-empty")
drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
return true

# a is d or a directory above d.
fn above(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> bool
var x = d
while x >= 0 bound 4096
if x == a
return true
x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
return false

# The child of a on the way down to d (a strictly above d).
fn child_towards(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> i64
var x = d
while fs.nodes[x as usize].parent != a bound 4096
x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
return x

pub fn rename_at(fs: &mut Fs, src: &text, dst: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
let o = try resolve(fs, src, false)
let n = try resolve(fs, dst, false)
if not named(&o) or not named(&n)
fail bad("busy")
if o.nd < 0
fail bad("no-entry")
let isdir = fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].dir
if not isdir and (o.slash or n.slash)
fail bad("not-directory")
# lock_rename's trap: the entry under the common ancestor
if o.dir != n.dir
if above(fs, o.dir, n.dir) and child_towards(fs, o.dir, n.dir) == o.nd
fail bad("invalid")

fail bad("not-empty")

return true

let tdir = fs.nodes[n.nd as usize].dir
if isdir and not tdir
fail bad("not-directory")
if not isdir and tdir
fail bad("is-directory")
if tdir and not is_empty(fs, n.nd)
fail bad("not-empty")
drop_ent(fs, n.dir, &n.last)
drop_ent(fs, o.dir, &o.last)
fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: n.dir, name: copy(n.last), nd: o.nd))
if isdir
fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].parent = n.dir
return true

# stat: "d" for a directory, else "f" and the size.
pub fn stat_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> text ! FsErr
let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
if w.nd < 0
fail bad("no-entry")
if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
return "d"
if w.slash
fail bad("not-directory")
return "f" + fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].data.len().tostr()

fn text_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
var i: usize = 0
while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 4096
if a[i] != b[i]
return a[i] < b[i]
i += 1
return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# The entry names of a directory, sorted (without "." and "..").
pub fn list_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> List[text] ! FsErr
let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
if w.nd < 0
fail bad("no-entry")
if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir

return o

var v: i64 = 0
for c in s.chars()
v = v * 10 + (c[0] as i64 - 48)
return v

return "ok"
if k == "open"
let h = try open_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
return "h" + h.tostr()

let s = try read(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
return "=" + s
if k == "write"
let _ = try write(fs, num(&a[1]), &a[2])
return "ok"
if k == "seek"
let _ = try seek(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
return "ok"
if k == "trunc"
let _ = try truncate(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
return "ok"
if k == "close"
let _ = try close(fs, num(&a[1]))
return "ok"

return "ok"
if k == "rmdir"

return "ok"

return try stat_at(fs, &a[1])

# outcome of each (ok, hN, =data, d, fN, :names or an error-code), joined by ";".
pub fn script(s: text) -> text
var fs = fs_new()
var out: List[text] = []
for line in s.split(";")
let a = line.split(" ")
out.push(op1(&mut fs, &a) catch |e| e.code)
return ";".join(out)

return "ok"

return "ok"

# Run a script of ";"-separated operations on a fresh filesystem; the
# outcome of each (ok, hN, =data, d, fN, :names or an error-code), joined by ";".
pub fn script(s: text) -> text
var fs = fs_new()
var out: List[text] = []
for line in s.split(";")
let a = line.split(" ")
out.push(op1(&mut fs, &a) catch |e| e.code)
return ";".join(out)

# program's authority is exactly its grants (Sandbox v0.1) and it never

var o = ""

v.push(0)

fail BadSignal(why: "invalid signal")

bsync = s
if best < 0
return none
if not is_rt(best)
p.std[best as usize] = false

var o: List[Queued] = []

module os.signal

# Signals (survey M40), pure. A signal never runs an asynchronous handler
# in a Form: the host takes it (blocked, then dequeued as signalfd or
# sigtimedwait does) and admits it as an event Signal(kind) at the next
# tick boundary. Sending one is cap Kill under grant exec.
# - The cross-OS table: each signal name with its number on Linux
# (x86, ARM and most others), Alpha/SPARC, MIPS and PA-RISC (signal(7))
# and on Darwin (xnu bsd/sys/signal.h), its default action and the
# standard that defines it.
# - glibc's strsignal text and bash's kill -l names on Linux.
# - Windows console control events and their nearest signal.
# - The pending-signal model the host uses to order admissions, as Linux
# keeps it: a standard signal is pending at most once (a second send
# while pending is dropped, the first value kept); a real-time signal
# (34 to 64) queues every send; setting a disposition that ignores a
# signal (SIG_IGN, or SIG_DFL for CONT, CHLD, WINCH, URG) discards its
# pending sends, yet a send to a blocked, ignored signal stays pending;
# sending SIGCONT discards pending stop signals and a stop signal
# discards a pending SIGCONT; dequeuing takes the synchronous signals
# (SEGV, BUS, ILL, TRAP, FPE, SYS) first, then the lowest number, and
# real-time instances in the order sent.

error BadSignal(why: text)

# alpha/sparc "29/-" lists Alpha then SPARC).

for c in s.chars()

pub fn number(name: &text, target: &text) -> i64 ! BadSignal
let r = try row(name)
if target == "linux"
return num(&r.linux)
if target == "darwin"
return num(&r.darwin)
if target == "mips"
return num(&r.mips)
if target == "parisc"
return num(&r.parisc)
if target == "alpha" or target == "sparc"
let p = r.alpha_sparc.split("/")
if p.len() == 1

pub fn action(name: &text) -> text ! BadSignal

pub fn standard(name: &text) -> text ! BadSignal
let r = try row(name)
return copy(r.standard)

# SIGIOT, SIGPOLL, SIGCLD, SIGUNUSED and on Linux SIGINFO, are not preferred); "" when there is none.

if n == RTMAX
return "RTMAX"

return "RTMAX-" + (RTMAX - n).tostr()
let lx = "linux"

if s == ""
return ""
let cs = s.chars()
var o = ""
var i: usize = 3
while i < cs.len() bound 64
o = o + cs[i]
i += 1
return o

pub fn strsignal(n: i64) -> text
if n >= 1 and n <= 31

# console program sees for them (SIGINT for Ctrl+C, SIGBREAK = 21 for the
# others); "" for an unknown event.
pub fn console_event(code: i64) -> text
if code == 0
return "CTRL_C_EVENT"
if code == 1
return "CTRL_BREAK_EVENT"
if code == 2
return "CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT"
if code == 5
return "CTRL_LOGOFF_EVENT"
if code == 6
return "CTRL_SHUTDOWN_EVENT"

pub fn console_signal(code: i64) -> i64
if code == 0
return 2
if code == 1 or code == 2 or code == 5 or code == 6
return 21
return -1

pub struct Queued

val: i64

pub struct Pending

stdval: List[i64]
rt: List[Queued]

pub fn pending_new() -> Pending

var v: List[i64] = []

b.push(false)
v.push(0)
k += 1

# Services (survey M44), pure: the supervision decisions a host makes for a
# service unit, as systemd makes them (src/shared/exit-status.c,
# src/basic/signal-util.c, src/core/service.c at systemd main, Oct 2026):
# - exit status names (SUCCESS, TEMPFAIL, NAMESPACE, ...) and their class
# (libc, systemd, LSB, BSD), and the exit status a of names;
# - signal names as systemd reads them: numbers, HUP or SIGHUP,
# RTMIN+n and RTMAX-n (Linux numbering: SIGRTMIN 34, SIGRTMAX 64);
# - SuccessExitStatus=, RestartPreventExitStatus= and
# RestartForceExitStatus= sets, with systemd's number syntax (decimal,
# 0x hex, C octal, 0o and 0b prefixes);
# - the result of a main process exit (clean, exit-code, signal,
# core-dump) and the Restart= decision with its reason;
# - launchd's KeepAlive decision (launchd.plist(5): a bool, or a dict of
# SuccessfulExit and Crashed conditions) and the Windows service
# control manager's failure actions (sc failure / sc failureflag),
# both recorded live (vectors/os/svc/launchd_keepalive.tsv on macOS
# 27.0.1, vectors/os/svc/scm_failure_actions.tsv on Windows build
# 26200).
# Codes and statuses are those of waitid(2): code "exited" with the exit
# status, "killed" or "dumped" with the signal number.

if scm_action(p, runs) != "restart"

module rand.det

# Deterministic random streams (survey M12). A generator is the RFC 8439
# ChaCha20 keystream under a 32-byte seed, so a run replays bit for bit
# from its seed. The library draws no entropy: fresh seed bytes enter a
# program as a logged host result, and `from_entropy` takes them only
# together with a `Cap[Entropy]` (5.16), which a program holds only while
# handling an event that carries it. `from_seed` is for seeds that are
# already part of the program or its log (test vectors, replays, a value
# split from another generator). Not for keys: this is reference code and
# not constant time; key material comes straight from logged Random bytes.
#
# Stream: key = the 32 seed bytes; nonce = stream id (bytes 0..7, little
# endian) followed by 4 zero bytes; block counter starts at 0. Blocks past
# 2^32 carry into the third nonce word, so for counters below 2^32 the
# output is exactly the RFC 8439 keystream. Words are taken in order and
# serialise little endian. Bytes are List[i64] with values 0..255; words
# are i64 masked to 32 bits.

v[b] = rotl32(v[b] ^ v[c], 12)

quarter(&mut x, 3, 7, 11, 15)

module time

# Time as a logged input (survey M10). There is no clock here: an instant
# is a number a program received in an event (a Tick, a host.WallTime
# result), and every function is pure arithmetic on it, so replay is exact.
# Instant: i64 nanoseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z on the POSIX
# timescale (no leap seconds; 23:59:60 is refused on parse). Duration: i64
# nanoseconds. Range: about years 1678..2261 for instants; day-level civil
# functions work on any i64 day count that fits. Overflow traps (checked
# integers). Civil dates are proleptic Gregorian, from Howard Hinnant's
# "chrono-Compatible Low-Level Date Algorithms" (days_from_civil,
# civil_from_days, weekday_from_days). Time zones need tz data as a logged
# or pinned input (see vectors/SOURCE.md); only fixed UTC offsets here.

pub const NS: i64 = 1
pub const US: i64 = 1000
pub const MS: i64 = 1000000
pub const SEC: i64 = 1000000000
pub const MINUTE: i64 = 60000000000
pub const HOUR: i64 = 3600000000000
pub const DAY: i64 = 86400000000000

pub struct Civil
y: i64
m: i64
d: i64

# floor division and modulo for possibly negative a, b > 0
pub fn fdiv(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 = if a >= 0 then a / b else 0 - ((0 - a - 1) / b) - 1

pub fn fmod(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 = a - fdiv(a, b) * b

# Days since 1970-01-01 of a proleptic Gregorian date (Hinnant).
pub fn days_from_civil(y0: i64, m: i64, d: i64) -> i64
let y = if m <= 2 then y0 - 1 else y0
let era = fdiv(y, 400)
let yoe = y - era * 400
let mp = if m > 2 then m - 3 else m + 9
let doy = (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + d - 1
let doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy
return era * 146097 + doe - 719468

pub fn civil_from_days(z0: i64) -> Civil
let z = z0 + 719468
let era = fdiv(z, 146097)
let doe = z - era * 146097
let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146096) / 365
let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100)
let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153
let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1
let m = if mp < 10 then mp + 3 else mp - 9
let y = yoe + era * 400 + (if m <= 2 then 1 else 0)
return Civil(y: y, m: m, d: d)

pub fn weekday_from_days(z: i64) -> i64 = if z >= -4 then (z + 4) % 7 else (z + 5) % 7 + 6

pub fn is_leap(y: i64) -> bool = fmod(y, 4) == 0 and (fmod(y, 100) != 0 or fmod(y, 400) == 0)

# Erratum E-1 to 6.7: a map iterates in  key order (7.1), never in
# insertion order. Keys are inserted out of order, overwritten and removed.
fn walk() -> text
var m: Map[text, u32] = {"pear": 1, "apple": 2}
m.insert("fig", 3)
m.insert("banana", 4)
m.insert("apple", 5)
let _ = m.remove("pear")
var s = ""
for (k, v) in m
s = s + k + "=" + v.tostr() + ";"
return s

fn ints() -> text
var m: Map[i64, text] = {}
m.insert(10, "x")
m.insert(-3, "y")
m.insert(2, "z")
var s = ""
for k in m.keys()
s = s + k.tostr() + ","
for v in m.values()
s = s + v
return s

check walk() == "apple=5;banana=4;fig=3;"
check ints() == "-3,2,10,yzx"
